So we muſtmust not onelyonly hate, and avoid groſſegross ſinssins, but every thing that may carry a ſavorsavoursavor, or ſuſpritionsuspicionsusprition of ſinsin; we muſtmust abhor the very ſignessigns and tokens of ſinsin; ſoso in Proverbs 5. ver. 8. Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the dooredoor of her houſehouse. He that would not be burnt muſtmust dread the fire; HeeHe that would not hearehear the bell, muſtmust not meddle with the rope. To venture upon the occaſionoccasion of ſinsin, and then to pray, lead us not intoOne ſaidsaid, as oft as I have been among vainevain men, I returned home leſſeless a man thenthan I was before. temptation, is all one, as to thruſtthrust thy finger into the fire, and then to pray that it might not be burnt. So in the 4. Prov. 14. 15. youYou have another command, Enter not in the path of the wicked, and goego not in the way of evellevil men, avoid it, and paſſepass not by it, turneturn from it, and paſſepass away. This triple gradation of Solomon
ſhewethshoweth with a great EmphaſieEmphasy, how neceſſarynecessary it is for men, to flee from all appearance of ſinsin: as the Sea-man ſhunsshuns ſandssands, and ſhelvesshelves, and as men ſhunshun thoſethose, that have the plague-ſoressores running upon them: as weeds doedo endanger the cornecorn, as bad humors • doedo endanger the bloudblood, or as an infected houſehouse doth indangerendanger the neighbourhood: ſoso doth the company of the bad endanger thoſethose that are good; intireneſſeentirenessintireness with wicked confortsconsorts, is one of the ſtrongeſtstrongest chaineschains of hell, and bindesbinds us to a participation, both of ſinsin and puniſhmentpunishment.

The ſecondsecond Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device2 Remedy. of Satan is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that ordinarily there is no conqueſtconquest over ſinsin, without the ſoulesoul turnesturns from the occaſionoccasion of ſinsin; 'tis’tis impoſſibleimpossible for that man to get the conqueſtconquest of ſinsin, that playesplays and ſportssports with the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin; God will not remove the tentationtemptation, exceptThe Fable ſaithsaith, that the ButterflieButterfly asked the OwleOwl how he ſhouldshould dealedeal with the fire, which had ſingedsinged her wings, who counſel'dcounsel'd her not to behold ſoso much as its ſmoaksmokesmoak. we turneturn from the occaſionoccasion. It is a juſtjust and righteous thing with God, that he ſhouldshould fall into the pit, that will adventure to dance upon the brink of the pit; and that he ſhouldshould be a ſlaveslave to ſinsin, that will not flee from the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin. As long as there is fuellfuel in our hearts for a temptation, we cannot be ſecuresecure; he that hath gun-powder about him, had need keep far enough off
from ſparklessparkles; to ruſhrush upon the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin, is both to tempt our ſelvesselves, and to tempt Satan to tempt our ſoulssouls; 'tis’tis very rare that any ſoulesoul playesplays with occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin, but that ſoulsoul is inſnar'densnar'dinsnar'd by ſinsin; 'tis’tis ſeldomeseldom that God keeps that ſoulsoul from the acts of ſinsin, that will not keep off from the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin; he that adventures upon the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin, is as he that would quench the fire with Oyleoil, which is a fuellfuel to maintainemaintain it; and increaſeincrease it. Ah ſoulssouls! oftenOften remember, how frequently you have been overcome by ſinsin, when you have boldly gongone upon the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin; look back ſoulssouls, to the days of your vanity, wherein you have been as eaſilyeasily conquered, as tempted, vanquiſhedvanquished, as aſſaultedassaulted, when you have played with the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin; and therefore, as you would for the future be kept from the acting of ſinsin, and be made victorious over ſinsin, oh flee from the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin.

The third Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice3 Remedy. of Satan, is ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider, that other precious Saintssaints that were once glorious on earth, and are now triumphing in heaven, have turned from the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin, as Hellhell it ſelfeself; as you may ſeesee in JoſephJoseph, Gen. 39. 10. And it came to paſſepass, as ſheshe ſpakespake to JoſephJoseph day by day, that he hearknedhearkened not unto her, to lyelie by
her, or to be with her. JoſephJoseph was famous for all the four Cardinallcardinal vertuesvirtues; if ever any were in this one temptation, you may ſeesee his Fortitudefortitude, Juſticejustice, Temperancetemperance,There are ſtoriesstories of Heathens, that would not look upon excellent beauties, leſtlest they ſhouldshould be inſnaredensnared. and Prudenceprudence, in that he ſhunsshuns the occaſionoccasion (for he would not ſoso much as be with her) and that a man is indeed, that he is in a temptation, which is but a tap to give vent to corruption. The Nazarite might not only not drink wine, but not taſtetaste a grape, or the husk of a grape. The LeaperLeper was to ſhaveshave his hairehair, and paireparepair his nailesnails. The Devilldevil counts a fit occaſionoccasion, halfehalf a conqueſtconquest; for he knowesknows that corrupt nature hath Democritus pluck't out his own eyes, to avoid the danger of uncleanneſſeuncleanness. a ſeedseed-plot of all ſinsin, which being drawn forth, and watered by ſomesome ſinfullsinful occaſionoccasion, is ſoonsoon ſetset a work to the producing of death and deſtructiondestruction; God will not remove the temptation, till we remove the occaſionoccasion. A Birdbird whiles a loftaloft, is ſafesafe, but ſheshe comes not near the ſnaresnare without danger; the ſhunningshunning the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin renders a man moſtmost like the beſtbest of men; a ſoulsoul eminently gracious, dares not come near the trainetrain, though he be far off the blow. So Job 31. 1. I made a Covenantcovenant with mine eyes,
ברית כרתי 〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉 I cut a Covenant; In making Covenants, it was a cuſtomecustom among the JewesJews, to cut ſomesome beaſtbeast or other in pieces, and to walk between the pieces, to ſignifiesignify, that they deſireddesired God to deſtroydestroy them that ſhouldshould break the Covenant. why then ſhouldshould I think upon a maid? window of the ſoulesoul, and if that ſhouldshould be alwayesalways open, the ſoulsoul might ſmartsmart for it. A man may not look intently upon that, that he may natnot love intirelyentirely. The Diſciplesdisciples were ſetset a goggagog, by beholding the beauty of the Templetemple; 'tis’tis beſtbest and ſafeſtsafest to have the eye alwayesalways fixtfixed upon the higheſthighest and nobleſtnoblest objects; as the Marrinersmariner'smariners eye is fixtfixed on the ſtarstar, when their hand is on the ſternesternsterne: ſoso David, when he was himſelfhimself, he ſhunsshuns the occaſionoccasion of ſinsin, PſalPsal. 26. 4, 5. I have not ſatsat with vainevain perſonspersons, neither will I goego in with diſſemblersdissemblers; I have hated the Congregationcongregation of evillevil doers, and will not ſitsit with the wicked. Stories ſpeakspeak of ſomesome that could not ſleepsleep, when they thought of the Trophiestrophies of other Worthiesworthies, that went before them; the higheſthighest and choyceſtchoicest examples are to ſomesome, and ſhouldshould be to all very quickningquickening and provoking; and oh! that the examples of thoſethose worthy Saintssaints, David, JoſephJoseph, and Job, might prevaileprevail with all your ſoulssouls to ſhunshun and avoid the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin; every one ſhouldshould ſtrivestrive to be like to them in grace, that they deſiredesire to be equallequal with in glory. He that ſhootethshooteth at the Sunsun, though he come far ſhortshort, will ſhootshoot higher, thenthan he that aimeth at a ſhrubshrub; 'tis’tis beſtbest (and it ſpeaksspeaks out much of ChriſtChrist within) to eye the higheſthighest,
and the worthieſtworthiest examples.

The fourth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice4 Remedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that the avoiding the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin, is an evidence of grace, and that which lifts up a man above moſtmost other men in the world; that a man is indeed, which he is in temptation; and when ſinfullsinful occaſionsoccasions doedo preſentpresent themſelvesthemselves before the ſoulsoul, this ſpeaksspeaks out both the truth, Plutarch ſaithsaith of DemoſthenesDemosthenes, that he was excellent at praiſingpraising the worthy acts of his AnceſtorsAncestors, but not ſoso at imitating them, oh that this were not applicable to many profeſſorsprofessors in our times. and the ſtrengthstrength of grace; when with Lot, a man can be chaſtchaste in SodomeSodom, and with Timothy can live temperately in AſiaAsia, among the luxurious EpheſiansEphesians; and with Job can walk uprightly in the land of ƲzUz, where the people were prophaneprofane in their lives, and ſuperſtitioussuperstitious in their worſhipworship; and with Daniel, be holy in Babylon; and with Abraham righteous in Chaldea; and with Nehemiah, zealous in DamaſcoDamasco, &etcc. Many a wicked man is big, and full of ſinfulsinful corruption, but ſhewsshows it not for want of occaſionoccasion; but that man is ſurelysurely good, who in his courſecourse will not be bad, though tempted by occaſionsoccasions; a ChriſtleſſeChristless ſoulsoul is ſoso far from refuſingrefusing occaſionsoccasions when they come in his way, that he looks and longs after them, and rather thenthan he will go without them, he will buy them not onelyonly with love or money, but alſoalso with the loſſeloss of his ſoulsoul; nothing
but grace can fence a man againſtagainst the occaſionsoccasions of ſinsin, when he is ſtronglystrongly tempted thereunto; therefore as you would cherriſhcherishcherrish a precious evidence in your own boſomesbosoms, of the truth and ſtrengthstrength of your graces, ſhunshun all ſinfullsinful occaſionsoccasions.

The eighteighth Devicedevice that Satan hath to8 Device. draw the ſoulesoul to ſinsin, is, by preſentingpresenting'Twas’Twas’twas a weighty ſayingsaying of Seneca (Nihil eſtest infelicius eo, cui nil nunquānunquamnunquamnunquan contigit adverſi • adversi; there is nothing more unhappy, thenthan he who never felt adverſityadversity. to the ſoulesoul the outward mercies, that vainevain men inioyenjoy, and the outward miſeriesmiseries, that they are freed from, whil'ſtwhil'st they have walked in the wayesways of ſinsin. Saith Satan, do'ſtdostdo'st thou not ſeesee oh ſoulesoul! theThe many mercies, that ſuchsuch and ſuchsuch inioyenjoy, that walk in thoſethose very wayesways, that thy ſoulsoul ſtartlesstartles to think of, and the many croſſescrosses that▪ they are delivered from, even ſuchsuch as makes other men (that ſaysay they dare not walkewalk in ſuchsuch wayesways) to ſpendspend their dayesdays in ſighingsighing, weeping, groaning, and mourning, and therefore ſaithsaith Satan, if ever thou wouldeſtwouldest be freed from the dark night of adverſityadversity, and injoyenjoy the ſunsun-ſhineshine of proſperityprosperity, thou muſtmust walk in their wayesways: by this ſtratagemstratagem the Devildevil took thoſethose in the 44 Jeremiah, 16, 17, 18. As for the word that thou haſthast ſpokenspoken unto us, in the name of the Lord, we will not hearken unto thee; but we will certainly doedo whatſoeverwhatsoever thing goeth forth of our mouth, to burneburn IncenſeIncense
unto the Queen of Heavenheaven, and to pour Some of the Heathens would be wicked as their Gods were, counting it a diſhonourdishonour to their God, to be unlike to him. Lactan tiusLactantius.
out drink-offringsofferings unto her, as we have done, we and our Fathers, our Kings, and our Princesprinces in the Citiescities of Judah, and in the ſtreetsstreets of JeruſalemJerusalem: for then had we plenty of victuallsvictuals, and were well, and ſawsaw no evillevil. But ſincesince we left off to burn IncenſeIncense to the Queen of Heavenheaven, and to pour out drink-offerings unto her, we have wanted all things, and have been conſumedconsumed by the ſwordsword, and by the famine. This is juſtjust the language of a world of ignorant, prophaneprofane, and ſuperſtitioussuperstitious ſoulssouls in London, and England, that would have made them a Captainecaptain'Tis’Tis’tis ſaidsaid of one of the EmperoursEmperors, that Rome had no war in his davesdays, becauſebecause 'twas’twas plague enou • gh to have ſuchsuch an EmperourEmperor; you are wiſewise, and know how to apply it. to returnereturn to bondage, yea to that bondage that was worſeworse thenthan that the IſraelitesIsraelites groaned under. Oh, ſaysay they, ſincesince ſuchsuch and ſuchsuch perſonspersons have beenebeen put down, and left off, we have had nothing but plundering and taxing, and butchering of men, &etcc. andAnd therefore we will doedo, as we and our Kings and Noblesnobles, and Fathers have formerly done; for then had we plenty at home, and peace abroad, &etcc. andAnd there was none to make us afraid.

div.head: Now the Remedies againſtagainst this Device of Satan, are theſethese that follow.
div.p:
THeThe firſtfirst Remedyremedy is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider,1 Remedy. that no man knowesknows how the heart of God ſtandsstands by his hand, his hand of mercy may be towards a man, when his heart may be ſetset againſtagainst that man; as you may ſeesee in Saul, and Tully judged the JewsJews' Religion to be naught, becauſebecause they were ſoso often overcome, & impoveriſh'dimpoverish'd, and afflicted; and the Religion of Rome to be right, becauſebecause the Romans proſperedprospered, and became Lords of the world; & yet though the Romans had his hand, the Jews had his heart; for they were dearly beloved, though ſorelysorely afflicted. others; and the hand of God may be ſetset againſtagainst a man, when the heart of God is dearly ſetset upon a man, as you may ſeesee in Job and Ephraim; the hand of God was ſorelysorely ſetset againſtagainst them, and yet the heart and bowels of God were ſtronglystrongly working towards them; no man knoweth either love or hatred, by outward mercy or miſerymisery; for all things come alike to all, to the righteous, and to the unrighteous; to the good, and to the bad, to the clean, and to the unclean, &etcc. The ſunsun of proſperityprosperity ſhinesshines as well upon brambles of the Wilderneſſewilderness, as fruit-trees of the Orchardorchard; the ſnowsnow and hailehail of adverſityadversity lights upon the beſtbest gardens, as well as the ſtinkingstinking dunghills, or the wild waſtewaste. AhabsAhab's and Joſiah'sJosiah's ends concur in the very circumſtancescircumstances. Saul and Jonathan, though different in their natures, deſertsdeserts, and deportments,
yet in their deaths they were not divided. Health, wealth, honours, &etcc. croſſescrossesCrosses, ſickneſſessicknesses, loſſeslosses, &etcc. areareAre caſtcast upon good men, and bad men promiſcuouſlypromiscuously. The whole TurkiſhTurkish Empireempire is Nihil eſtest niſinisi mica panis. Luther. nothing elſeelse but a cruſtcrust, caſtcast by Heavensheaven'sheavens great HouſeHouse-keeper to his dogs. MoſesMoses dies in the Wilderneſſewilderness, as well as thoſethose that murmured; Nabal is rich, aſwellas well as Abraham; AchitophellAchitophel wiſewise, aſwellas well as Solomon; and Doeg honoured by SoulSaulsoul, as well as IoſephJoseph was by PharoahPharaoh. UſuallyUsually the worſtworst of men have moſtmost of theſethese outward things, and the beſtbest of men have leaſtleast of Earthearth, though moſtmost of Heavenheaven.

The ſecondsecond Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice2 Remedy. of Satan, is, ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider, That there is nothing in the world that doth ſoso provoke God to be wrathwroth, and angry, as mensmen's taking incouragementencouragement from GodsGod's goodneſſegoodness, and mercy, to do wickedly; this you may ſeesee by that wrath that fell upon the old world, and by GodsGod's raining hell out of Heavenheaven uponSuch ſoulessouls make God a God of clouts, one that will not doedo as he ſaithsaith, but they ſhallshall find God to be as ſeveresevere in puniſhingpunishing, as he is to others gracious in pardoning. Good turnesturns aggravate unkindneſſesunkindness, and our guilt is increaſedincreased by our obligations. SodomeSodom and GomorahGomorrah. This is clear in that 44 of Jeremiah, from the 20 verſeverse, to the 28 verſeverse, the words are worthy of your beſtbest meditation; oh that they were engraven in all your hearts, and conſtantconstant in all your thoughts! thoughThough they are too large for me to tranſcribetranscribe them, yet they are not too large for you to remember
them: To argue from mercy to ſinfullsinful liberty, is the Devilsdevil'sdevils Logicklogic, and ſuchsuch Logicianslogicians doedo ever walk, as upon a mine of Gungun-powder, ready to be blown up; no ſuchsuch ſoulssouls can ever avert, or avoid the wrath of God. This is wickedneſſewickedness at the height, for a man to be very bad, becauſebecause God is very good, a worſeworse ſpiritspirit thenthan this is not in hell; ah Lord! dothDoth not wrath, yea the greateſtgreatest wrath, lie at this mansman's door? Are not the ſtrongeſtstrongest chaineschains of darknesdarkness prepared for ſuchsuch a ſoulsoul? To ſinsin againſtagainst mercy, is to ſinsin againſtagainst humanity, it is beſtiallbestial, nay it is worſeworse. To render good for evillevil, is Divinedivine, to render good for good, is humanehuman, to render evillevil for evillevil, is brutiſhbrutish; but to render evillevil for good, is deviliſhdevilish; and from this evillevil deliver my ſoulsoul oh God.

The third Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice3 Remdy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that there is no greater miſerymisery in this life, thenthan not to be in miſerymisery; no greater Religio peperit divitias & filia devoravit matrem. Ephraim is joynedjoined to Idolsidols, let him alone. Why ſhouldshould you be ſmittensmitten any more, you will revolt more and more. When the Phyſicianphysician gives over the Patientpatient, you ſaysay
ring out his knell, the man is dead: ſoso when God gives over a ſoulsoul to ſinsin, without controulecontrol, you may truly ſaysay, this ſoulesoul is loſtlost; you may ring out his knelknell, for he is twice dead, and pluckt up by the roots. FreedomeFreedom from puniſhmentpunishment is the mother of ſecuritysecurity, the ſtepstep-mother of virtue, the poyſonpoison of Religionreligion, the moth of holineſſeholiness, and the introducer of wickedneſſewickedness; nothing ſaidsaid one, ſeemesseems more unhappy to me, thenthan he to whom no adverſityadversity hath happened. Outward mercies oft-times prove a ſnaresnare to our ſoulessouls. I will lay a ſtumblingstumbling block, Ezek. 3. 20. Vatablus his note there isFaciam, ut omnia habeant proſperaprospera; calamitatibus eum à peccato non revocabo. I will proſperprosper him in all things, and not by affliction, reſtrainerestrain him from ſinsin. ProſperityProsperity hath been a ſtumblingstumbling block, at which millions have ſtumbledstumbled, and fallen, and broke the neck of their ſoulssouls for ever.

The fourth Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device4 Remedy. of Satan, is ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider, that the wants of wicked men under all their outward mercy, & freedom from adverſitieadversity, is far greater thenthan alall their outward injoymentsenjoyments. They have many mercies, yet they want more thenthan they injoyenjoy; the mercies which they injoyenjoy are nothing to the mercies they want; 'Tis’tis true, they have honors, and riches, and pleaſurespleasures and friends, and are mighty in power,
their ſeedseed is eſtabliſhedestablished in their ſightsight with them, and their off-ſpringspring before their eyes; their houſeshouses are ſafesafe from fearefear, neither is the rod of God upon them; They ſendsend forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance. They take the TimbrellTimbrel and Harpharp, and rejoycerejoice at the Men that injoyenjoy all worldly comforts, may truly ſaysay, Omnes humanae conjolationesconsolationes ſuntsunt deſolationesdesolationes.

They want acceptation and reconciliation with God; They want Righteouſneſſerighteousness, Juſtificationjustification, Sanctificationsanctification, Adoptionadoption, and Redemptionredemption. They want the pardon of ſinsin, and power againſtagainst ſinsin, and freedomefreedom from the dominion of ſinsin: They want that favour that is better thenthan life, and that joy that is unſpeakableunspeakable and full of glory; and that peace that paſſespasses underſtandingunderstanding; and that Nec ChriſtusChristus nec coelum pati▪ turpatitur hyperbolen, Neither ChriſtChrist, nor Heaven, can be hyperbolized. grace, the leaſtleast ſparkspark of which, is more worth thenthan Heavenheaven and Earthearth. They want a HouſeHouse that hath foundations, whoſewhose builder and maker is God; they want thoſethose riches that periſhperish not; that
glory that fades not, that Kingdomekingdom that ſhakesshakes not. Wicked men are the moſtmost needy men in the world, yea, they want thoſethose two things that ſhouldshould render their mercies ſweetsweet, viz. The bleſſingblessing of God, and content with their condition; and without which, their Heavenheaven is but Hellhell, on this ſideside Hellhell: When their hearts are lifted up, and grown big upon the thoughts of their abundance; if conſcienceconscience do'sdoes but putA crownecrown of gold cannot cur • e the head achheadache, nor a velvet ſlipperslipper cannot eaſeease the Gout, no mor • e can honour or riches, &etcc. quiet and ſtillstill the ConſcienceConscience. The heart of man is a three ſquaresquare triangle, which the whole round circle of the world cannot fill (as Mathematicians ſaysay) but all the corners will complainecomplain of e • mptinesemptiness and hunger for ſomt • hingsomethingsomthing elſeelse. in a word, and ſaysay, 'tis’tis true, here is this and that outward mercy, oh! but where is an intereſtinterest in ChriſtChrist? Where is the favour of God? Where are the comforts of the holy GhoſtGhost? Where are thy evidences for Heavenheaven, &etcc.? This word from Conſcienceconscience makes the mansman's countenance to change, his thoughts to be troubled, his heart to be amazed, and all his mercies on the right hand, and left, to be as dead and withered. Ah! were but the eyes of wicked men open to ſeesee their wants, under their abundance, they would cry out, and ſaysay as AbſalomAbsalom did, What are all theſethese to me, ſoso long as I cannot ſeesee the KingsKing's face? What's honour, and riches, and the favour of Creaturescreatures, ſoso long as I want the favour of God, the pardon of my ſinssins, an intereſtininterest ininterestin ChriſtChrist, and the hopes of glory. O IodGodJod, give me theſethese, or I dyedie, give
me theſethese, or elſeelse I ſhallshall eternally dyedie.

The fiftfifth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice5 Remedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to confiderconsider, that outward things are not as they ſeemseem, and are eſteemedesteemed; they have indeed a glorious outſideoutside, but if you view their inſidesinsides, you will eaſilyeasily find that they fill the head full of cares, and the heart full of fearesfears; what if the fire ſhouldshould conſumeconsume one part of my eſtateestate, and the ſeasea ſhouldshould be a grave to ſwallowswallow up another part of my eſtateestate; what if my ſervantsservants ſhouldshould be unfaithfullunfaithful abroad, and my children ſhouldshould be deceitful at home? ahAh the ſecretsecret fretting, vexing, and gnawing, that doth daily, yea hourly, attend thoſethose mensmen's ſoulssouls, whoſewhose hands are full of worldly goods. 'Twas’Twas a good ſpeechspeech of an Emperouremperor, you (ſaidsaid he) gaze on my purple Roberobe, a • nd golden Crowncrown, but did you know what cares are under it, you would not take it up from the ground to have it. 'Twas’Twas a true ſayingsaying of AuguſtineAugustine on the 26 PſalmPsalm, many are Multi amando res noxias ſuntsunt miſerimiseri, habendo miſerioresmiseriores. AuguſtAugust. miſerablemiserable by loving hurtfullhurtful things, but they are more miſerablemiserable by having them. It is not what men injoyenjoy, but the principle from whence it comes, that makes men happy; much of theſethese outward things doedo uſuallyusually cauſecause great diſtractiondistraction, great vexation, and great condemnation at laſtlast, to the poſeſſorspossessorsposessors of
them; if God gives them in his wrath, & do not ſanctifiesanctify them in his love, they will at laſtlast be witneſſeswitnesses againſtagainst a man, and racks to torture and torment a man, and milſtonesmillstones for ever to ſinksink a man, in that day, when God ſhallshall call men to an account, not for the uſeuse, but for the abuſeabuse of mercy.

The ſixtsixth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice6 Remedy. of Satan, is, ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider the end and the deſignedesign of God, in heaping up mercy upon the heads of the wicked, and in giving them (a quietus eſtest) reſtrest Valerian the Roman EmperourEmperor, fell from being an EmperourEmperor, to be a foot-ſtoolstool to Sapor, King of PerſiaPersia. DionyſiusDionysius King of Sicily, fell from his Kingly glory, to be a School-maſtermaster. The brave Queen Zenobia was brought to Rome in golden chaineschains. and quiet from thoſethose ſorrowssorrows and ſufferingssufferings that others ſighsigh under. David in that 73 PſalPsal. 17, 18, 19, 20 verſesverses, ſhewsshows the end and deſignedesign of God in this, ſaithsaith he, When I went into the Sanctuary of God, then I underſtoodunderstood their end: Surely thou diddeſtdidstdiddest ſetset them in ſlipperyslippery places: thou caſtedſtcastedst them downedown into deſtructiondestruction. How are they brought into deſolationdesolation as in a moment, they are utterly conſumedconsumed with terrors. As a dreamedream when one awaketh, ſoso, O Lord, when thou awakeſtawakest: thou ſhaltshalt deſpiſedespise their image. So in the 92 PſalPsal. 7. When the wicked ſpringspring as graſſegrass, and when all the workers of iniquity doedo flouriſhflourish, it is that they ſhallshall be deſtroyeddestroyed for ever. GodsGod's ſettingsetting them up, is but in order to his caſtingcasting them down; his raiſingraising them high, is but in order to his bringing
them low. Exod. 9. 16. And in very deed, for this cauſecause have I raiſedraised thee up, for to ſhewshow in thee my power, and that my name may
Valens an EmperourEmperor, BeliſariusBelisarius a famous general, Henry the 4th4th, Bajazeth, Pythias, Great Pompey, and William the Conqueror; theſethese from being very high, were brought very low; they all fell from great glory and majeſtymajesty, to great poverty and miſerymisery Da Domine ut ſicsic poſſideamuspossideamus temporalia ut non perdamus aeterna. Bern. Grant us Lord that we may ſoso partake of temporalltemporal felicity, that we may not loſelose eternalleternal. be declared throughout all the earth. I have conſtitutedconstituted and ſetset thee up as a But-mark, that I may let fliefly at thee, and follow thee cloſeclose with plague upon plague, till I have beaten the very breath out of thy body, and got my ſelfself a name, in ſettingsetting my feet upon the neck of all thy pride, power, pomp, and glory. Ah ſoulessouls! whatWhat man in his wits would be lifted up, that he might be caſtcast down, would be ſetset higher thenthan others, when 'tis’tis but in order to his being brought downedown lower thenthan others. There is not a wicked man in the world, that is ſetset up with Lucifer, as high as Heavenheaven, but ſhallshall with Lucifer be brought down as low as Hellhell. CanſtCanst thou think ſeriouſlyseriously of this oh ſoulsoul? andAnd not ſaysay, O Lord, I humbly crave that thou wilt let me be little in this world, that I may be great in another world; and low here, that I may be high for ever hereafter: Let me be low, and feed low, and live low, ſoso I may live with thee for ever; let me now be cloathedclothed with rags, ſoso thou wilt cloathclothe me at laſtlast with thy Robesrobes; let me now be ſetset upon a dunghill, ſoso I may at laſtlast be advanc'd to ſitsit with thee • upon thy Thronethrone; Lord, make me rather
gracious, thenthan great; inwardly holy, thenthan outwardly happy; and rather turn me into my firſtfirst nothing, yea, make me worſeworse thenthan nothing, rather thenthan ſetset me up for a time, that thou mayeſtmayest bring me low for ever.

The ſeventhseventh Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice7 Remedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that God doth often moſtmost plague and puniſhpunish thoſethose, whom others think he doth moſtmost ſparespare and love; that is, God do'sdoes plague and puniſhpunish them moſtmost with ſpirituallspiritual judgements (which are the greateſtgreatest, the ſoreſtsorest, and the heavieſtheaviest) whom he leaſtleast puniſhespunishes with temporalltemporal puniſhmentspunishments; there are no men on earth PſalPsal. 81. 12. PſalPsal. 78. 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31. PſalPsal. 106. 15. He gave them their requeſtrequest, but ſentsent leanneſſeleanness into their ſoulesoul. 'Tis’Tis’tis a heavy plague to have a fat body, and a lean ſoulsoul; a houſehouse full of gold, and a heart full of ſinsin. ſoso internally plagued, as thoſethose that meet with leaſtleast externallexternal plagues. Oh! the blindneſſeblindness of mind, the hardneſſehardness of heart, the ſearedneſſesearedness of Conſcienceconscience, that thoſethose ſoulssouls are given up to, who in the eye of the world, are reputed the moſtmost happy men, becauſebecause they are not outwardly afflicted and plagued as other men. Ah ſoulssouls! 'twere’Twere better that all the temporalltemporal plagues that ever befell the children of men ſincesince the fall of Adam, ſhouldshould at once meet upon your ſoulssouls, thenthan that you ſhouldshould be given up to the leaſtleast ſpirituallspiritual plague, to the leaſtleast meaſuremeasure of ſpirituallspiritual blindneſſeblindness, or ſpirituallspiritual hardneſſehardness of heart, &etcc. nothingNothing
will better that man, nor move that man, that is given up to ſpirituallspiritual judgements; let God ſmilesmile or frownefrown, ſtrokestroke, or ſtrikestrike, cut or kill, he minds it'Tis’Tis’tis better to have a ſoresore, thenthan a ſearedseared conſcienceconscience. 'Tis’Tis’tis better to have no heart thenthan a hard heart; no mind, thenthan a blind mind. not, he regards it not; let life, or death, heaven, or hell, be ſetset before him, it ſtirsstirs him not, he is made up onmad upon his ſinsin, and God is fully ſetset to doedo Juſticejustice upon his ſoulesoul; this mansman's preſervationpreservation, is but a reſervationreservation unto a greater condemnation. This man can ſetset no bounds to himſelfehimself, he is become a brat of fathomleſſefathomless perdition. He hath guilt in his boſomebosom, and vengeance at his back, whereeverwherever he goes; neither miniſtryministry, nor miſerymisery, neither miracle, nor mercy, can mollifiemollify his heart; and if this ſoulsoul be not in hell on this ſideside hell, who is? whoWho is?8 Remedy.

The eigtheighth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice of Satan, is, to dwell more upon that ſtrictstrict account that vain men muſtmust make for all that good that they doedo injoyenjoy,In this day men ſhallshall give an account (De bonis commiſſiscommissis, de bonis dimiſſisdimissis, de malis commiſſiscommissis, de malis permiſſispermissis) of good things committed unto them, of good things neglected by them, of evils committed by them, and of evillsevils ſufferedsuffered by them. thenthan upon the outward good they doedo injoyenjoy. Ah! did men dwell more upon that account, that they muſtmust ere long give for all the mercies that they have injoyedenjoyed, and for all the favours that they have abuſedabused, and for all the ſinssins they have committed,, it would make their hearts to tremble, and their lips to quiver, rottenneſſerottenness to enter into their
bones; it would cauſecause their ſoulessouls to cry out, and ſaysay, oh! that our mercies had been fewer, and leſſerlesser, that our account might have been eaſiereasier, and our torment and miſerymisery (for our abuſeabuse of ſoso great mercy) not greater thenthan we are able to bear. O curſedcursed be the day wherein the Crowncrown of honour was ſetset upon our heads, and the treaſurestreasures of this world were caſtcast into our laps; O curſedcursed be the day wherein the ſunsun of proſperityprosperity ſhin'dshin'd ſoso ſtrongstrong upon us, and this flattering world ſmil'dsmil'd ſoso much upon us, as to occaſionoccasion us to forget God, to ſlightslight JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist, to neglect our ſoulssouls, and to put far from us the day of our account. Philip the third of SpaineSpain, whoſewhose life was free from groſſegross evillsevils, profeſſedprofessed, that he would rather looſeloseloose all his Kingdomekingdom, thenthan offend God willingly; yet being in the Agonyagony of death, and conſideringconsidering more throughlythoroughly of his In die judicii plus valebit conſcientiaconscientia pura, quam marſupiamarsupia plena. Bernard. Then ſhallshall a good conſcienceconscience be more worth thenthan all the worldsworld's good. account he was to give to God, fearefear ſtruckstruck into him, and theſethese words brake from him; Oh! would to God I had never reigned; oh that thoſethose years I have ſpentspent in my Kingdomekingdom, I had lived a life in the wilderneſſewilderness! ohOh that I had lived a ſolitarysolitary life with God! howHow much more ſecurelysecurely ſhouldshould I now have dyeddied? howHow much more confidently ſhouldshould I have gone to the Thronethrone of
God? What doth all my glory profit me, but that I have ſoso much the more torment in my death. God keeps an exact account of every penny that's laid out upon him, and his, and that is laid out againſtagainst him, and his; and this in the day of account, men ſhallshall know and feel, though now they wink, and HieromeJerome ſtillstill thought that that voycevoice was in his ears (Surgite mortui & venite ad judicium) AriſeArise you dead, and come to judgement. As oft as I think on that day, how doth my whole body quake, and my heart within me tremble? will not underſtandunderstand. The ſleepingsleeping of vengeance, cauſethcauseth the overflowing of ſinsin, and the overflow of ſinsin cauſethcauseth the awaking of vengeance; abuſedabused mercy will certainly turn into fury; GodsGod's forbearance is no quittance; the day is at hand, when he will pay wicked men for the abuſeabuse of new and old mercies; if he ſeemseem to be ſlowslow, yet he is ſuresure: he hath leaden heels, but iron hands; the farther he fetcheth his blow, or draweth his arrow, the deeper he will wound in the day of vengeance. MensMen's actions are all in print in heaven, and God will, in the day of account, read them aloud, in the ears of all the world, that they may all ſaysay amen to that righteous ſentencesentence that he ſhallshall paſſepass upon all the deſpiſersdespisers and abuſersabusers of mercy.

The ninth Devicedevice that Satan hath to9 Device. draw the ſoulesoul to ſinsin, is, by preſentingpresenting to the ſoulesoul, the croſſescrosses, loſſeslosses, reproaches, ſorrowssorrows, and ſufferingssufferings, that doedo daily attend thoſethose that walk in the
wayesways of holineſſeholiness. Saith Satan, do not you ſeesee that there are none in the world that are ſoso vexed, afflicted, and toſſedtossed, as thoſethose that walk more circumſpectlycircumspectly, and holily thenthan their neighbours; they are a by-word at home, and a reproach abroad; their miſeriesmiseries come in upon them, like Job's meſſengersmessengers, one upon the neck of another; and there is no end of their ſorrowessorrows and troubles; therefore ſaithsaith Satan, you were better walk in wayesways that are leſſeless troubleſometroublesome, and leſſeless afflicted, though they be more ſinfullsinful; for who but a mad man would ſpendspend his dayesdays in ſorrowsorrow, vexation, and affliction, when it may be prevented, by walking in the wayesways that I ſetset before him.

div.head: Now the Remedies againſtagainst this device of Satan are theſethese that follow.
div.p:
THeThe firſtfirst Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice1 Remedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that all the afflictions that doedo attend the people of God, are ſuchsuch, as ſhallshall turneturn to the profit, and glorious advantage of the people of God; they ſhallshall diſcoverdiscover that filthineſſefilthiness and vileneſſevileness in ſinsin, that yet the ſoulsoul hath never ſeenseen. It was a ſpeechspeech of a GermaneGerman
Divinedivine, in his ſickneſſesickness; In this DiſeaſediseaseGuſparGasparGuspar Olevianus. I have learned how great God is, and what the evillevil of ſinsin is; I never knew to purpoſepurpose what God was before, nor what ſinsin meant till now. Afflictions are a chriſtallcrystalchristall glaſſeglass, wherein the ſoulsoul hath the cleareſtclearest ſightsight of the ugly face of ſinsin; in this glaſſeglass the ſoulsoul comes to ſeesee ſinsin to be but a bitter-ſweetsweet; yea, in this glaſſeglass the ſoulsoul comes to ſeesee ſinsin, not only to be an evillevil, but to be the greateſtgreatest evillevil in the world, to be an evillevil far worſeworse then helthan hell.

AgaineAgain, they ſhallshall contribute to theIſaIsa. 1. 25. c. 27. 8, 9. mortifying and purging away of their ſinssins; afflictions are GodsGod's furnace, by which he cleanſescleanses his people from their droſſedross; affliction is a fire, to purge outIn times of peace our Armerarmour is ruſtyrusty, in time of war 'tis’tis bright. our droſſedross, and to make virtue ſhineshine; it is a potion to carry away ill humours; better thenthan all the Benedicta MedicamentumMedicamenta, as Phyſitiansphysicians call them. Aloes kills worms, colds and froſtsfrosts doedo deſtroydestroy VermineVermin: ſoso doedo afflictions the corruptions that be in our hearts. The JewesJews under all the Prophetsprophets thundering, retained their Idolsidols; but after their babyloniſhBabylonishbabylonish captivity, 'tis’tis obſervedobserved, there have been no Idolsidols found amongſtamongst them.

Again, afflictions are ſweetsweet preſervativespreservatives to keep the Saintssaints from ſinsin, which is a greater evillevil thenthan hell it ſelfself: as Job
ſpakespake, Surely it is meet to be ſaidsaid unto God, Job 34. 31, 32 I have borne chaſtiſementchastisement, I will not offend any more. Anaxagoras, had not theſethese things periſhedperished, I could not have been ſafesafe, ſaidsaid this PhiloſopherPhilosopher, when he ſawsaw great poſſesſionspossessions that he had loſtlost. ſoulessouls ſhallshall ſaysay, we would not for all the world, but that weewe had met with ſuchsuch, and ſuchsuch troubles, and afflictions; for ſurelysurely, had not theſethese befallen us, it would have been worſeworse, and worſeworse with us; Oh! the carnal ſecuritysecurity, pride, formality, dead-heartedneſſeheartedness, lukewarmneſſelukewarmness, cenſoriouſneſſecensoriousness, and earthlineſſeearthliness, that God hath cured us of, by the troubles and dangers that we have met with, in the wayesways and ſervicesservices of the Lord. I remember a ſtorystory of a godly man, that as heehe was going to take ſhippingshipping for France, he broke his leg, and it pleaſedpleased Providenceprovidence ſoso to order it, that the ſhipship that he ſhouldshould have gone in, at that very time, was caſtcast away, and not a man ſavedsaved; ſoso by breaking a bone, his life was ſavedsaved. So the Lord many times breaks our bones, but 'tis’tis in order to the ſavingsaving of our lives, and our ſoulessouls for ever; he gives us a potion that makes us heart-ſicksick, but 'tis’tis in order to the making us perfectly well, and to the purging of us from thoſethose ill humours, that have made our heads akeache, and GodsGod's heart akeache, and our ſoulssouls ſicksick, and heavy to the death, &etcc. div.head: The third Device that Satan3. Device. hath to hinder ſoulessouls from holy and heavenly ſervicesservices, from gracious, and religious performances, is,

A ſoulesoul not ſtir'dstir'd by this, not rais'd, and lifted up by this, to be reſoluteresolute and brave in the ſerviceservice of God, notwithſtandingnotwithstanding all dangers and difficulties, is a ſoulesoul left of God to much blindneſſeblindness, and hardneſſehardness.

The 4. Remedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice of4. RemedieRemedy. Satan, is, to conſiderconsider, that religious duties, holy and heavenly exerciſesexercises are
only difficult to the worſerworser, to the ignoble part of a Saintsaint; they are not to the noble, and better part of a Saintsaint, to the noble part, the ſoulesoul, and the renewed affections of a Saintsaint; holy exerciſesexercises are a heavenly pleaſurepleasure, and recreation, as the Apoſtleapostle ſpeaksspeaks, I delight in the Lawlaw of God, after the inward As every flowrflower hath its ſweetsweet ſavoursavour, ſoso every good duty carries meat in the mouth, comfort in the performance of it. χρηστὸς 〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉

To the noble part of a Saintsaint, ChriſtsChrist's yoke is eaſieeasy, and his burden is light; all the commands and wayesways of ChriſtChrist (even thoſethose that tend to the pulling out of right eyes, and cutting off of right hands) are joyous, and not grievous to the noble part of a Saintsaint; all the wayesways and ſervicesservices of ChriſtChrist are pleaſantneſſepleasantness (in the abſtractabstract) to the better part of a Saintsaint; a Saintsaint, ſoso far as he is renewed, is alwayesalways beſtbest, when he ſeessees moſtmost of God, when he taſtstastes moſtmost of God, when he is higheſthighest in his injoymentsenjoyments of God, and moſtmost warmewarm, and lively in the ſerviceservice of God; oh! ſaithsaith the noble part of a Saintsaint, that it might be alwayesalways thus; oh! that my ſtrengthstrength were the ſtrengthstrength of ſtonesstones, and my fleſhflesh as braſſebrass, that my worſerworser part might be more ſerviceableserviceable to my noble part, that I might act by an untired power in that ſerviceservice, that is a pleaſurepleasure, a ParadiſeParadise to me.

The fifth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice5 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that great reward, and glorious recompencerecompense that doth attend thoſethose that cleave to the ſerviceservice of the Lord, in the BaſilBasil ſpeaksspeaks of ſomesome Martyrs that were caſtcast out all night naked, in a cold froſtyfrosty time, &and were to be burned the next day, how they comforted themſelvesthemselves in this manner; The winter is ſharpsharp, but ParadiſeParadise is ſweetsweet; here we ſhivershiver for cold, but the boſomebosom of Abraham will make amends for all. face of all difficulties, and diſcouragementsdiscouragements; though the work be hard, yet the wage • s is great, Heavenheaven will make amends for all, I, one hourshour's being in heaven will abundantly recompencerecompense you for cleaving to the Lord, and his wayesways, in the face of all difficulties. This carried the Apoſtleapostle through the greateſtgreatest difficulties; heehe had an eye to the recompencerecompense of reward; he look't for a houſehouse that had foundations, whoſewhose builder and maker was God, and for a heavenly countreycountry; yea, this bore up the Spirit of ChriſtChrist, in the face of all difficulties and diſcouragementsdiscouragements: Looking unto JeſusJesus the author and finiſherfinisher of our faith, who for the joy that was ſetset before him, endured the Croſſecross, deſpiſingdespising the ſhameshame, and is ſetset downedown at the right hand of the Thronethrone of God.

ChriſtiansChristians that would hold on in the ſerviceservice of the Lord, muſtmust look more upon the Crowncrown, thenthan upon the Croſſecross; more upon their future glory, thenthan their preſentpresent miſerymisery; more upon their incouragementsencouragements, thenthan upon their diſcouragementsdiscouragements. GodsGod's very ſerviceservice is wages, his wayesways are ſtrewedstrewed with roſesroses,
and paved with joy that is unſpeakableunspeakable,This is praemium ante praemium, a ſuresure reward of welwell doing, in doing thereof (not only for doing thereof) there is great reward, PſalPsal. 19. v. 11. and fulfull of glory, and with peace that paſſethpasseth underſtandingunderstanding. Some degree of comfort follows every good action; as heateheat accompanies fire, as beamesbeams and influences iſſueissue from the Sunsun. Moreover by them is thy ſervantservant warned, and in keeping of them there is great reward; not only for keeping, but in keeping of them, there is great reward; the joy, the reſtrest, the refreſhingrefreshing, the comforts, the contents, the ſmilessmiles, the incomes that Saintssaints now injoyenjoy in the wayesways of God, are ſoso precious and glorious in their eyes, that they would not exchange them for ten thouſandthousand worlds; Ah! if the vailesvails be thus ſweetsweet and glorious before pay-day comes, what will be that glory, that ChriſtChrist will crown his Saintssaints with, for cleaving to his ſerviceservice in the face of all difficulties: When he ſhallshall ſaysay to his father, LoeLo here am I, and the children which thou haſthast given me; if there be ſoso much to be had in a wilderneſſewilderness, what then ſhallshall be had in ParadiſeParadise? &etcc.

div.head: The fourth Device that Satan4 Device. hath to keep ſoulessouls off from holy exerciſesexercises, from religious ſervicesservices, is,
div.p: BYBy working them to make falſefalse inferences, from thoſethose bleſſedblessed and glorious things that ChriſtChrist hath done; As that JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist hath done all for us; therefore there is nothing for us to doedo, but to joy, and rejoycerejoice, he hath perfectly juſtifiedjustified us, and fulfilled the Lawlaw, and ſatisfiedsatisfied divine Juſticejustice, and pacified his FathersFather's wrath, and is gone to Heavenheaven to prepare a place for us, and in the mean time, to intercede for us; and therefore away with praying, and mourning, and hearing, &etcc. Ah! what a world of Profeſſorsprofessors hath Satan drawn in theſethese dayesdays, from religious ſervicesservices, by working them to make ſuchsuch ſadsad, wildewild, and ſtrangestrange inferences, from the ſweetsweet and excellent things, that the Lord JeſusJesus hath done for his beloved ones.

div.head: Now the Remedies againſtagainst this device of Satan are theſethese that follow.

THeThe firſtfirst Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device1. RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, to dwell as much on thoſethose Scriptures that ſhewshow you the duties and ſervicesservices that ChriſtChrist requires of you, as upon thoſethose Scriptures that declare Tertullian hath this expreſſionexpression of the fulneſſefulness of the Scriptures (Adoro plenitudinem Scripturarum) I adore the fulneſſefulness of the Scripture. Now a ſoulesoul that would not be drawn away by this device of Satan, heehe muſtmust not look with a ſquintsquint eye upon theſethese bleſſedblessed Scriptures, and abundance more of like import; but he muſtmust dwell upon them, he muſtmust make theſethese Scriptures to be his chiefeſtchiefest, and his choiſeſtchoicest companions, and this will be a happy meanesmeans to keep him cloſeclose to ChriſtChrist, and his ſerviceservice in theſethese times, wherein many turn their backs upon ChriſtChrist, under pretence of being highly intereſtedinterested in the great and glorious things that have been acted by ChriſtChrist, &etcc.

The ſecondsecond Remedieremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice2. RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, to conſiderconsider, that the great and glorious things that JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist hath done, and is a doing for us, ſhouldshould be ſoso far from taking us off from religious ſervicesservices, and pious performances, that they ſhouldshould be the greateſtgreatest motives and encouragements to the performance of them that may be, as the Scriptures do abundantly evidence. I 1 Pet. 2. 9. Luke 1. 74, 75. The third Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device3. Remedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that thoſethose precious ſoulssouls which JeſusJesus ChriſtChristThe Saints Motto in all ages hath been (Laboremus) let's be doing. hath done, and ſufferedsuffered as much for, as he hath for you, have been exceeding active and lively in all religious ſervicesservices, and heavenly performances; he did as much, and ſufferedsuffered as much for David, God loves (curriſtascurristas, not quariſtasquaristas) the runner, not the queſtionerquestioner, or diſputerdisputer, ſaithsaith Luther. as • for you, and yet, who more in praying, and prayſingpraisingpraysing God thenthan David? ſevenSeven

The fourth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this device4. Remedy. of Satan, is, ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider this,
that thoſethose that doedo not walk in ways of righteouſneſſerighteousness and holinesholiness (that do not wait upon God in the ſeveralseveral duties and ſervicesservices that are commanded by him) cannot have that evidence to their own ſoulessouls of their righteouſneſſerighteousness before God, of their fellowſhipfellowship and communionCertainly 'tis’tis one thing to judgjudge by our graces, another thing to reſtrest, or put our truſttrust in them. div.head: The fifth Device that Satan5. Device. hath to draw ſoulessouls off from religious ſervicesservices, and to keep ſoulessouls off from holy duties, and heavenly performances, is,

The ſecondsecond Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device2. RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, to conſiderconsider, that in all ages God hath had ſomesome that have been great, rich, wiſewise, and honourable, that have choſenchosen his wayesways, and cleaved to his ſerviceservice in the face of all difficulties,Good Nobles (ſaithsaith one) are like black ſwansswans, and thinly ſcatteredscattered in the firmament of a ſtatestate, even like ſtarsstars in the firſtfirst ma • gnitude, yet ſomesome God hath had in alall ages, as might be ſhewedshowed out of HiſtoriesHistories. though not many wiſewise men, yet ſomesome wiſewise men have; and though not many mighty, yet ſomesome mighty have; and though not many noble, yet ſomesome noble have; witneſſewitness Abraham, and Jacob, and Job, and ſeverallseveral Kings, and others that the Scriptures ſpeakspeak of; and ah! how many have we among our ſelvesselves, whoſewhose ſoulessouls have cleaved to the Lord, and who have ſwumswum to his ſerviceservice, through the blood of the ſlainslain, and who havehave not counted their lives dear unto them, that they and others might injoyenjoy the holy things of ChriſtChrist, according to the mind and heart of ChriſtChrist, &etcc.

ChriſtChrist in this life will not free any beleeverbeliever from the preſencepresence of any one ſinsin, though he doth free every beleeverbeliever from the damning power of every ſinsin; There's no condemnation to them that are in ChriſtChrist JeſusJesus, who walkewalk not after the fleſhflesh, but after the ſpiritspirit. The Lawlaw cannot condemn a beleeverbeliever, for ChriſtChrist hath fulfilled it for him; divine Juſticejustice cannot condemn him, for that ChriſtChrist hath ſatisfiedsatisfied; his ſinnssins cannot condemcondemn him, for they in the blood of ChriſtChrist are pardoned; and his owneown conſcienceconscience (upon righteous grounds) cannot condemn him, becauſebecause ChriſtChrist, that is greater thenthan his conſcienceconscience, hath acquitted him, &etcc.
