The fourth Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device of Satan, is, to look upon all your ſinssins, as charged upon the account of ChriſtChrist, as debts which the Lord JeſusJesus hath fully ſatisfiedsatisfied; and indeed were there but one farthing of that debt unpaid, that ChriſtChrist was engaged to ſatiſfiesatisfy, it would not have ſtoodstood with the unſpottedunspotted juſticejustice of God, to have let him come into Heavenheaven, and ſitsit down at his owneown right hand; but all our debts by his death being diſchargeddischarged, we are freed, and he is exalted to ſitsit down at the right
hand of his Father, which is the top of his glory, and the greateſtgreatest pledgpledge of our felicity; For he hath made him to be ſinsin for
2 Cor. 5. 21. ChriſtChrist was (peccatorum maximus) the greateſtgreatest of ſinnerssinners by imputation, and reputation. IſaIsa. 53. 5, 6.
us that knew no ſinnesin, that we might be made the righteouſneſſerighteousness of God in him, ſaithsaith the Apoſtleapostle: All our ſinssins were made to meetemeet upon ChriſtChrist, as that Evangelicallevangelical Prophetprophet hath it. He was wounded for our tranſgreſſionstransgressions, he was bruiſedbruised for our iniquities, the chaſtiſementchastisement of our peace was upon him, and with his ſtripesstripes we are healed. All we like ſheepsheep have gone aſtrayastray, we have turned every one to his owneown way, and the Lord hath laydlaid on him the iniquity of us all; or as the Hebrew hath it, he hath made the iniquity of us all to meet in him. In Lawlaw we know, that all the debts of the Wifewife are charged upon the Husband; ſaithsaith the Wifewife to one, and to another, ifChriſtChrist hath the greateſtgreatest worth and wealth in him, as the worth and value of many pieces of ſilversilver is in one piece of gold, ſoso all the excellencies ſcatteredscattered abroad in the creatures, are united to ChriſtChrist. I owe you any thing, go to my husband; ſoso may a beleeverbeliever ſaysay to the Lawlaw, and to the juſticejustice of God; if I owe you any thing, go to my ChriſtChrist, who hath undertaken for me; I muſtmust not ſitsit downedown diſcourageddiscouraged under the apprehenſionsapprehensions of thoſethose debts, that ChriſtChrist to the utmoſtutmost farthing hath fully ſatisfiedsatisfied; would it not argue much weakneſſeweakness, I had almoſtalmost ſaidsaid much madneſſemadness, for a debtor to ſitsit down diſcourageddiscouraged, upon his looking over thoſethose debts, that his ſuretysurety hath readily, freely, and fully ſatisfiedsatisfied; the ſenſesense
of his great love ſhouldshould engage a man forAll the whole volume of perfections, which is ſpreadspread through Heaven & earth, is epitomized in him. ever to love, and honour his ſuretysurety, and to bleſſebless that hand that hath paid the debt, and croſtcrossed the books, &etcc. butBut to ſitsit down diſcourageddiscouraged when the debt is ſatisfiedsatisfied, is a ſinnnesinsinnne that beſpeaksbespeaks Repentancerepentance, &etcc.

ChriſtChrist hath cleared all reckonings betwixt God and us; you remember the Scape-goategoat, upon his head all the iniquities Levit. 16. 21. of the children of IſraelIsrael, and all their tranſgreſſionstransgressions in all their ſinnssins were confeſſedconfessed ChriſtChrist is (Canalis gratiae) the channellchannel of grace from God. and put, and the Goategoat did bearebear upon him all their iniquities, &etcc. Why, the Lord JeſusJesus is that bleſſedblessed Scape-Goategoat, upon whom all our ſinssins were laid, and who alone hath carried our ſinssins away into the Landland of forget fulneſſefulnessforgetfulness, where they ſhallshall never, never be remembredremembered more; a beleeverbeliever under the guilt of his ſinsin may lookelook the Lord in the face, and ſweetlysweetly plead thus with him; 'Tis’tis true Lord, I owed theeThe bloods of Abel, for ſoso the Hebrew hath it (as if the blood of one Abel had ſoso many tongues as drops) cryedcried for vengeance againſtagainst ſinnesin; bu • t the blood of ChriſtChrist cries louder for the pa • rdon of ſinsin. much, but thy Son was my Ranſomeransom, my Redemptionredemption; his blood was the price, he was my ſuretysurety, and undertook to anſweranswer for my ſinnessins; I know thou muſtmust be ſatisfiedsatisfied, and ChriſtChrist hath ſatisfiedsatisfied thee to the utmoſtutmost farthing, not for himſelfhimself, for what ſinssins had he of his own? butBut for me, they were my debts that he ſatisfiedsatisfied for; be pleaſedpleased to look over the book, and thou ſhaltshalt find that 'tis’tis croſtcrossed
by thy owneown hand, upon this very account that ChriſtChrist hath ſufferedsuffered, and ſatisfiedsatisfied for them.

The fifth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this device5 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider of the reaſonsreasons, why the Lord is pleaſedpleased to have his people exerciſedexercised, troubled, and vexed with the operations of ſinfulsinful corruptions, AuguſtinAugustineAugustin ſaithsaith, that the firſtfirst, ſecondsecond, and third vertuevirtue of a ChriſtianChristian is humility. and they are theſethese; partly to keep them humble, and low in their owneown eyes; and partly to put them upon the uſeuse of all divine helps, whereby ſinsin may be ſubduedsubdued and mortified; And partly, that they may live upon ChriſtChrist for the perfecting the work of Sanctificationsanctification; Lilmod lelammed, we therefore learn, that weewe may teach, is a proverb among the Rabbins. After the Trojans had been wandering, & toſſingtossing up and down the Mediterranean Sea; as ſoonsoon as they eſpiedespied Italy, they cried out with exulting joy, Italy, Italy: ſoso will Saints when they come to Heaven. and partly, to weanewean them from things below, and to make them heart-ſicksick of their abſenceabsence from ChriſtChrist, and to maintain in them bowels of compaſſioncompassion towards others, that are ſubjectsubject to the ſamesame infirmities with them; and that they may diſtinguiſhdistinguish between a ſtatestate of grace, and a ſtatestate of glory, and that Heavenheaven may be more ſweetsweet to them in the cloſeclose. Now doth the Lord upon theſethese weighty reaſonsreasons ſuffersuffer his people to be exerciſedexercised, and moleſtedmolested with the operations of ſinfullsinful corruptions; oh! then let no beleeverbeliever ſpeakspeak, write, or conclude bitter things againſtagainst his owneown ſoulesoul, and comforts; becauſebecause that ſinnesin troubles and vexes his righteous ſoulesoul,
&etcc. butBut lay his hand upon his mouth, and be ſilentsilent, becauſebecause the Lord will have it ſoso, upon ſuchsuch weighty grounds, as the ſoulesoul is not able to withſtandwithstand.

The ſixthsixth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice6. Remedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that Beleeversbelievers muſtmust repent for their beingGod never ga • ve a BeleeverBeliever a new he • art, that it ſhouldshould always lie • a bleeding, and that it ſhouldshould always be rent and torn in pieces with diſcouragementsdiscouragements. diſcourageddiscouraged by their ſinssins. Their being diſcourageddiscouraged by their ſinssins will coſtcost them many a prayer, many a tearetear, and many a groanegroan: And that, becauſebecause their diſcouragementsdiscouragements under ſinsin flowesflows from ignorance and unbeliefeunbelief; it ſpringssprings from their ignorance of the riches, freeneſſefreeness, fulneſſefulness, and everlaſtingneſſeeverlastingness of GodsGod's love; and from their ignorance of the power, glory, ſufficiencysufficiency, and efficacy of the death and ſufferingssufferings of the Lord JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist: And from their ignorance of the worth, glory, fulneſſefulness, largeneſſelargeness, and compleatneſſecompletenesscompleatness of the righteouſneſſerighteousness of JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist: And from their ignorance of that reallreal, cloſeclose, ſpiritualspiritual, glorious, and inſeparableinseparable union that is betwixt ChriſtChrist, and their precious ſoulesoul: Ah! did precious ſoulssouls know, and beleevebelieve the truth of theſethese things, as they ſhouldshould, they would not ſitsit down dejected, and over-whelmed under the ſenſesense and operations of ſinsin, &etcc.

div.head: The ſecondsecond Device that Satan2 Device. hath to keep ſoulssouls in a ſadsad, doubting, and questioning condition, is,
div.p: BY working them to make falſefalse definitions of their graces: Satan knows, that as falſefalse definitions of ſinnesin wrong the ſoulesoul one way, ſoso falſefalse definitions of grace wrong the ſoulesoul another way.

I will inſtanceinstance only in faith; oh! how doth Satan labour might and main to work men to make falſefalse definitions of faith; Some he works to define faith too high, as that it is a full aſſuranceassurance of the love of God to a mansman's ſoulesoul in particular, or a full perſwaſionpersuasion of the pardon, and remiſſionremission of a mansman's owneown ſinssins in particular; ſaithsaith Satan, what doſtdost thou talk of faith? faithFaith is an aſſuranceassurance of the love of God, and of the pardon of ſinsin, and this thou haſthast not; thou knoweſtknowest thou art far off from this, therefore thou haſthast no faith; and by drawing men to make ſuchsuch a falſefalse definition of faith, he keeps them in a ſadsad, doubting, and queſtioningquestioning condition, and makes them ſpendspend their days in ſorrowsorrow and ſighingsighing,
ſoso that tearestears are their drink, and ſorrowsorrow is their meatemeat, and ſighingsighing is their work all the day long, &etcc.

The Philoſophersphilosophers ſaysay there are eight de • grees of heat; we diſcerndiscern three; now if • a ma • n ſhouldshould define heat only by the higheſthighest degree, then all other degrees will be caſtcast out from being heat: ſoso if men ſhallshall define fait • h only by the higheſthighest degrees, by aſſuranceassurance of the love of God, and of the pardon of his ſinssins in particular, what will become of leſſerlesser degrees of faith?

If a man ſhouldshould define a man to be a living man, onelyonly by the higheſthighest and ſtr • ongeſtstrongest demonſtrationsdemonstrations of life, as laughing, leaping, running, working, walking, &etcc. wouldWould not many thouſandsthousands that groan under internal, and externallexternal weakneſſesweaknesses, and that cannot laugh, nor leap, nor run, nor work, nor walk, be found dead men by ſuchsuch a definition, that yet weewe know to be alive; 'tis’tis ſoso here, and you know how to apply it, &etcc.

div.head: Now the Remedies againſtagainst this device of Satan are theſethese that follow.
div.p:
THeThe firſtfirst Remedieremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice1. Remedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly t • o conſiderconsider, that there may be true faith, yea, gr • eat meaſuresmeasures of faith, where there is no aſſuranceassurance. The Canaanite woman in the Goſpelgospel had ſtrongstrong faith, yet no aſſuranceassurance that we read of. TheſeThese things have I written unto you (ſaithsaith John) that believe on the name of the Son of God, that yeeye may know, that ye have eternalleternal life,, and that ye may beleevebelieve on the name of the Son of God; In theſethese words you ſeesee that they did believe, and had eternalleternal life, in reſpectrespect of the purpoſepurpose and promiſepromise of God, and in reſpectrespect of the ſeedsseeds, and beginnings of it in their ſoulssouls; and in reſpectrespect of ChriſtChrist their head, who ſitssits in Heavenheaven as a publiquepublic perſonperson, repreſentingrepresenting all his choſenchosen ones; Who hath raiſedraised us up together, EpheſEphes. 2. 6. and made us ſitsit together in heavenly places in ChriſtChrist JeſusJesus; and yet they did not know that they had eternalleternal life. 'Tis’Tis one thing to have a right to heaven, and another thing to know it; 'Tis’tis one thing to be beloved, and another thing for a
man to know that he is beloved. 'Tis’Tis one thing for God to write a mansman's name in the book of life, and another thing for God to tell a man, that his name is written in the book of life, and to ſaysay to him, rejoycerejoice, becauſebecause thy name is written in heaven.

So Paul: In whom yeeye alſoalso truſtedtrusted after
EpheſEphes 1. 13. So thoſethose in t • hat •
IſaIsa. 50. 10 had faith, though they had no aſſuranceassurance. Mica 7. 8, 9.
yeeye heard the word of truth, the Goſpellgospel of your ſalvationsalvation, in whom alſoalso after that yeeye believed, yeeye were ſealedsealed with that holy ſpiritspirit of promiſepromise.

So Micha, RejoyceRejoice not againſtagainst me oh my enemieenemy, when I ſhallshall fall, I ſhallshall riſerise; when I ſhallshall ſitsit in darkneſſedarkness, the Lord ſhallshall be a light unto me. I will bearebear the indignation of the Lord, becauſebecause I have ſinnedsinned, &etcc. orOr the ſadsad countenance of God, as the Hebrew hath it. This ſoulsoul had no aſſuranceassurance, for he ſitssits in darkneſſedarkness, and was under the ſadsad countenance of God, and yet had ſtrongstrong faith: As appears in thoſethose words, when I fall, I ſhallshall ariſearise: when I ſitsit in darkneſſedarkness, the Lord ſhallshall be a light unto me. He will bring me forth to the light, and I ſhallshall behold his righteouſneſſerighteousness, and let this ſufficesuffice for the firſtfirst anſweranswer.

The ſecondsecond Remedieremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice2. RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that God in the Scriptures doth defineJohn 1. 12. faith otherwiſeotherwise; God defines faith to be a re •• ceiving of ChriſtChrist; As many as received
him, to them he gave this priviledgeprivilege to be Act. 11. 23. the ſonssons of God, to as many as beleevedbelieved on his name; to be a cleaving of the ſoulesoul unto God, though no joy but afflictions attend the ſoulesoul. Yea, the Lord defines faith to be a coming to God in ChriſtChrist,Mat. 11. 28. John 6. 37. Heb. 7. 25., 26. IſaIsa.. 26. 3., 4, &etcc. and often to a reſtingresting, and ſtayingstaying, or roulingrolling of the ſoulesoul upon ChriſtChrist. 'Tis’Tis ſafeſtsafest, and ſweeteſtsweetest to define as God defines, both vices and graces; this is the only way to ſettlesettle the ſoulesoul, and to ſecuresecure it againſtagainst all the wiles of men and devillsdevils, who labour by falſefalse definitions of grace to keepekeep precious ſoulessouls in a doubting, ſtaggeringstaggering, and languiſhinglanguishing condition, and ſoso make their lives a burden, a hell unto them.

The third Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device3 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider this, that there may be true faith, where thereMat. 6. 30. chap. 14. 31. & chap. 16. 8. is much doubtings; witneſſewitness thoſethose frequent ſayingssayings of ChriſtChrist to his Diſciplesdisciples, Why are yeeye afraid oh yeeye of little faith? Luke 12. 28. PerſonsPersons may be truly believing, who nevertheleſſenevertheless are ſometimessometimes doubting; in the ſamesame perſonspersons (that the fore-mentioned Scriptures ſpeakspeak of) you may ſeesee their faith commended, and their doubts condemned, which doth neceſſarilynecessarily ſuppoſesuppose a preſencepresence of both.

The fourth Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device4 Remedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider,
that aſſuranceassurance is an effect of faith; therefore it cannot be faith. The cauſecause cannot be the effect, nor the root the fruit; as the effect ſlowesflowsslows from the cauſecause, the fruit from the root, the ſtreamstream from the fountain, ſoso doth the aſſuranceassurance flow from faith; this truth I ſhallshall make good thus.

The aſſuranceassurance of our ſalvationsalvation, and pardon of ſinsin doth primarily ariſearise from the witneſſewitness of the ſpiritspirit of God, thatEpheſEphes. 1. 13. Gal. 5. 6. we are the children of God: And the ſpiritspirit never witneſſethwitnesseth this, till we are beleeversbelievers; for we are ſonnessons by faith in Gal. 44. 6. ChriſtChrist JeſusJesus: therefore aſſuranceassurance is not faith, but followesfollows it, as the effect follows the cauſecause.

AgaineAgain, no man can be aſſuredassured, and perſwadedpersuaded of his ſalvationsalvation, till he be united to ChriſtChrist, till he be ingrafted into ChriſtChrist; and a man cannot be ingrafted into ChriſtChrist, till he hath faith; heehe muſtmust firſtfirst be ingrafted into ChriſtChrist by faith, before he can have aſſuranceassurance of his ſalvationsalvation, which doth clearly evidence, that aſſuranceassurance is not faith, but an effect and fruit of faith, &etcc.

Again, faith cannot be loſtlost, but aſſuranceassurance may; therefore aſſuranceassurance is not faith. Though aſſuranceassurance be a preciousPſalPsal. 51. 12. PſalPsal. 30. 6, 7. flower in the garden of a Saintsaint, and is more infinitely ſweetsweet, and delightful to
the ſoulesoul, thenthan all outward comforts,Cant. 5. 6. IſaIsa. 8. 17. and contents; yet 'tis’tis but a flower that is ſubjectsubject to fade, and to looſeloseloose its freſhneſſefreshness,There is many thouſandthousand precious ſoulssouls, of whom this world is not worthy, that have the f • aith of reliance, & yet want aſſuranceassurance, and the effects of it; as high joy, glorious peace, and vehement longings after the coming of ChriſtChrist. and beauty, as Saintssaints by ſadsad experience findefind, &etcc.

AgaineAgain, a man muſtmust firſtfirst have faith, before he can have aſſuranceassurance, therefore aſſuranceassurance is not faith; and that a man muſtmust firſtfirst have faith, before he can have aſſuranceassurance, is cleareclear; by this a man muſtmust firſtfirst be ſavedsaved, before he can be aſſuredassured of his ſalvationsalvation, for he cannot be aſſuredassured of that which is not; and a man muſtmust firſtfirst have a ſavingsaving faith, before he can be ſavedsaved by faith; for he cannot be ſavedsaved by that which he hath not; therefore a man muſtmust firſtfirst have faith, before he can have aſſuranceassurance, and ſoso it roundly followesfollows, that aſſuranceassurance is not faith, &etcc.

div.head: The third Device that Satan3 Device. hath to keepekeep the ſoulsoul in a ſadsad, doubting, and queſtioningquestioning condition, is,
div.p:
BY working the ſoulesoul to make falſefalsePſalPsal. 77. 7. 11. PſalPsal. 88. 1. ult. PſalPsal. 73. 2. 23. inferences from the croſſecross actings of providence; ſaithsaith Satan, doſtdost thou not ſeesee how Providenceprovidence croſſescrosses thy prayers,
and croſſescrosses thy deſiresdesires, thy tearestears, thy hopes, thy endeavours; ſurelysurely, if his love were toward thee, if his ſoulesoul did delight and take pleaſurepleasure in thee, he would not dealedeal thus with thee, &etcc.

div.head: Now the remedies againſtagainst this Device of Satan are theſethese that follow.
div.p:
THeThe firſtfirst Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device1 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider that many things may be croſſecross to our deſiresdesires, that are not croſſecross to our good; Abraham, Jacob, David, Job, MoſesMoses, Jeremiah, The Circumcellians being not able to withſtandwithstand the preaching, & writing of AuguſtineAugustine, ſoughtsought his deſtructiondestruction, having beſetbeset the way he was to goego his viſitationvisitation, but by GodsGod's providence, he miſſingmissing his way, eſcapedescaped the danger. Jonah, Paul, &etcc. metMet with many things that were contrary to their de firesdesires, and endeavours, that were not contrary to their good, as all know, that have wiſelywisely compared their deſiresdesires and endeavours, and GodsGod's actings together. PhyſickPhysic often works contrary to the Patientspatient'spatients deſiresdesires, when it doth not work contrary to their good. I remember a ſtorystory of a godly man, who had a great deſiredesire to goego to France, and as he was going to take ſhippingshipping, he broke his leg, and it pleaſedpleased providence ſoso to order it, that the ſhipship that he ſhouldshould have gone in, at that very ſamesame time was
caſtcast away, and not a man ſavedsaved, and ſoso by breaking a bone, his life was ſavedsaved. Though Providenceprovidence did workework croſſecross to his deſiresdesires, yet it did not work croſscross to his good, &etcc.

The ſecondsecond Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device2 Remedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that the hand of God may be againſtagainst a man, when the love and heart of God is much ſetset upon a man; No man can conclude how the heart of God ſtandsstands by his hand. The hand of God was againſtagainst Ephraim, and yet his love, his heart was IerJer. 31. 18, 19, 20. GodsGod's providentiallprovidential hand may be with perſonspersons, when his heart is ſetset againſtagainst them; GodsGod's providentiallprovidential hand was for a time with Saul, Haman, AſhurAshur, & IehuJehu, and yet his heart was ſetset againſtagainst them. No man knoweth love or hatred by all that is before them. EccleſEccles. 9. 1, 2. dearly ſetset upon Ephraim. I have ſurelysurely heard Ephraim bemoaning himſelfehimself thus; thou haſthast chaſtiſedchastised meeme, and I was chaſtiſedchastised as a bullockebullock unaccuſtomedunaccustomed to the yoke: turn thou me, and I ſhallshall be turned, for thou art the Lord my God. Surely after that I was turned, I repented; and after that I was inſtructedinstructed, I ſmotesmote upon my thigh; I was aſhamedashamed, yea, even confounded, becauſebecause I did bearebear the reproach of my youth. Ephraim is my dearedear ſonneson, he is a pleaſantpleasant child; for ſincesince I ſpakespake againſtagainst him, I doedo earneſtlyearnestly remember him ſtillstill: therefore my bowellsbowels are troubled for him, I will ſurelysurely have mercy upon him, ſaithsaith the Lord.

God can look ſowrlysourly, and chide bitterly, and ſtrikestrike heavily, even where, and when he loves dearly. The hand of God was very much againſtagainst Job, and yet
his love, his heart was very much ſetset upon Job, as you may ſeesee by comparing the 2. firſtfirstFirst chap. ofofOf IobJob with the two laſtlast. The hand of God was ſoresore againſtagainst David, and Jonah, when his heart was much ſetset upon them. He that ſhallshall conclude, that the heart of God is againſtagainst thoſethose that his hand is againſtagainst, will condemnecondemn the generation of the juſtjust, whom God unjuſtlyunjustly would not have condemned.

The third Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device3 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, to conſiderconsider, that all the croſſecross providences that befall the Saintssaints, are but in order to ſomesome noble good, that God doth intend to conferreconfer upon them. Providence wrotewrought croſſecross to DavidsDavid's deſiredesire, in taking away the child ſinfullysinfully begotten, but yet not croſſecross to a more noble good; for was it not farrefar better for David to have ſuchsuch a legitimate Heireheir as Solomon was, thenthan that a Baſtardbastard ſhouldshould wearewear the Crowncrown, and ſwaysway the Scepterscepter?

JoſephJoseph you know, was ſoldsold into a far Countrycountry by the envy and malice of his brethren, and afterwards impriſonedimprisoned, becauſebecause he would not be a priſonerprisoner to his MiſtriſſesMistress'sMistresses luſtslusts; yet all theſethese croſscross providences did wonderfully conduce to his advancement, and the preſervationpreservation of his FathersFather's family, which was then the viſiblevisible Churchchurch of ChriſtChrist. It was ſoso
ordered by a noble hand of providence, that what they ſoughtsought to decline, they did promote; JoſephJoseph was therefore ſoldsold by his brethren, that he might not be worſhippedworshipped, and yet he was therefore worſhippedworshipped, becauſebecause he was ſoldsold.

David was deſigneddesigned to a Kingdomekingdom; but oh the ſtraitsstraits, troubles, and deaths, that he run through, before he feels the weight of the Crowncrown; and all this was but in order to the ſweetningsweetening of his Crowncrown, and to the ſetlingsettling of it more firmly and gloriouſlygloriously upon his head; God did ſoso contrive it, that Jonah's offence, and thoſethose croſſecross actings of his that did attend it, ſhouldshould advantage that end which they ſeemedseemed moſtmost directlyThe motions of divine providence are ſoso dark, ſoso deep, ſoso changeable, that the wiſeſtwisest and nobleſtnoblest ſoulessouls cannot tell what concluſionsconclusions to make. to oppoſeoppose; Jonah he flies to TanſhiſhTarshishTanshish, then caſtcast into the Sea, then ſavedsaved by a miracle: Then the Marrinersmariners, as is very probable, who caſtcast Jonah into the Sea, declared to the NinivitesNinevites what had hapnedhappened; therefore he muſtmust be a man ſentsent of God, and that his threatningsthreatenings muſtmust be beleevedbelieved, and hearknedhearkened to, and therefore they muſtmust repent, and humble themſelvesthemselves, that the wrath threatnedthreatened might not be executed, &etcc.

The fourth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this device4 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider, that all the ſtrangestrange, dark, deep, and changeable providences that Believersbelievers
meet with, ſhallshall further them in their way to heaven, in their journey to happineſſehappiness; divine wiſdomewisdom and love will ſoso order all things here below, that they ſhallshall work for the reallreal, internallinternal, and eternalleternal good of them that love him. All the rugged providences that David met with, did contribute to the OroſiusOrosius ſpeakingspeaking of Valentinian, ſaithsaith, he that for ChriſtsChrist's name ſakesake had loſtlost a Tribune ſhipshiptribuneship, within a while after ſucceededsucceeded his perſecutorpersecutor in the Empire. bringing of him to the Thronethrone; and all the rugged promiſesprovidencespromises that Daniel, and the three children met with, did contribute to their great advancement; So all the rugged providences that Believersbelievers meet with, they ſhallshall all contribute to the lifting up of their ſoulessouls, above all things below God. As the waters lifted up Noah's Arkark nearer Heavenheaven: and as all the ſtonesstones that were about StevensStephen's earesears, did but knock him the cloſercloser to ChriſtChrist, the corner-ſtonestone, ſoso all the ſtrangestrange rugged providences that we meet with, they ſhallshall raiſeraise us nearer Heavenheaven, and knock us neerernearer to ChriſtChrist, that precious corner-ſtonestone, &etcc.

div.head: The fourth Device that Satan4 Device. hath to keep the ſoulesoul in a ſadsad, doubting, & queſtioningquestioning condition, is,
div.p: BY ſuggeſtingsuggesting to them, that their graces are not true, but counterfeit; ſaithsaith Satan, all is not gold that gliſtersglisters, all is not grace that you count grace, that you call grace; that whichYet it muſtmust be granted, that many a fair flower may grow out of a ſtinkingstinking root, and many ſweetsweet diſpoſitionsdispositions, and fair actions may be where there is onelyonly the corrupt root of nature. you call faith is but a fancy, and that which you call zeal, is but unnaturallunnatural heat and paſſionpassion; and that light you have, 'tis’tis but common, 'tis’tis ſhortshort to what many have attained to, that are now in hell, &etcc. Satan doth not labour more mightily to perſwadepersuade hypocrites that their graces are true, when they are counterfeit, thenthan he doth to perſwadepersuade precious ſoulssouls that their graces are counterfeit, when indeed they are true, and ſuchsuch as will abide the touch-ſtonestone of ChriſtChrist, &etcc.

div.head: Now the Remedies againſtagainst this device of Satan are theſethese that follow.
div.p: THeThe firſtfirst Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device of Satan, is, ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider, that grace is taken two wayesways.

FirſtFirst, 'tis’tis taken for the gracious good will and favour of God, whereby he is pleaſedpleased of his owneown free love, to accept of ſomesome in ChriſtChrist for his owneown. This ſomesome call the firſtfirst grace, becauſebecause 'tis’tis the fountainefountain of all other graces, and the Springspring from whence they flow; and it's therefore called grace, becauſebecause it makes a man gracious with God, but this is only in God.
Secondly, grace is taken for the gifts of grace, and they are of two ſortssorts, common, or ſpecialspecial.
Some are common to Beleeversbelievers, and hypocrites, as a gift of knowledge, a gift of prayer, &etcc.Gal. 5. 22, 23.
Some are ſpecialspecial graces, and they are proper, and peculiar to the Saintssaints, as faith, humility, meekneſſemeekness, love, patience, &etcc.

The ſecondsecond Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device2 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, wiſelywisely to conſiderconsider the
differences betwixt renuingrenewing grace, andGod brings not a pairepair of ſcalesscales to weigh our graces, but a touch-ſtonestone to try our graces. Purity, preciouſneſspreciousness, & holinesholiness is ſtamptstampt upon all ſavingsaving graces. Acts 15. 9. 2 Pet. 1. 1. IudeJude 20. reſtrainingrestraining grace; betwixt ſanctifyngsanctifyingsanctifyng grace, and temporary grace, and this I ſhallshall ſhewshow you in theſethese following particulars

1. True grace makes all glorious within and without. The KingsKing's daughter is all glorious within, her raiment is of wrought gold. True grace makes the underaſtandingunderstandingunderastanding glorious, the will glorious, the affections glorious, it caſtscasts a generallgeneral glory upon all the noble parts of the ſoulesoul; The KingsKing's daughter is all glorious within: And as it makes the inſideinside glorious, ſoso it makes the out-ſideside glorious; Her cloathingclothing is of wrought gold; it makes men lookelook gloriouſlygloriously, and ſpeakspeak gloriouſlygloriously, and walkewalk, and act gloriouſlygloriously: ſoso that vainevain ſoulssouls ſhallshall be Acts 4. verſvers. 8. to verſvers. 15. forced to ſaysay, that theſethese are they that have ſeenseen JeſusJesus; as grace is a fire to burn up, and conſumeconsume the droſſedross, and filth of the ſoulesoul, ſoso it is an ornament to 2 Cor. 5. 17. Καινὴ κτίσις 〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉 , a new creation, new Adam, new Covenant, new ParadiſeParadise, new Creation, new Lord, new Law, new hearts, & new natures go together▪. beautifiebeautify and adorn the ſoulesoul. True grace makes all new, the inſideinside new, and the out-ſideside new; If any man be in ChriſtChrist he is a new creature; but temporary grace doth not this. True grace changes the very nature of a man, morallmoral vertuevirtue doth only reſtrainrestrain, or chain up the outward man; it doth not change the whole man; a Lionlion in a
grate is a Lionlion ſtillstill, he is reſtrainedrestrained, but not changed; for he retains his Lionlion-like nature ſtillstill: ſoso temporary graces reſtrainerestrain many men from this and that wickedneſswickedness, but it doth not change and turn their hearts from wickedneſſewickedness; but now true grace, that turnesturns a Lionlion into a Lamb, as you may ſeesee in Paul, Acts 9. and a notorious ſtrumpetstrumpet, into a bleſſedblessed and glorious Penitentpenitent, as you may ſeesee in Mary Magdalen, &etcc. Luke 7.

2. The objects of true grace are ſupernaturallsupernatural; true grace is converſantconversant about the choiſeſtchoicest, and the higheſthighest objects, 2 Cor. 4. 18. chapHebr. 11. HebrProv. 15. Prov. 1424. A Saint hath his feet where other mensmen's heads are. Matth. 6. about the moſtmost ſoulsoul-enobling, and ſoulsoul-greatning objects, as God, ChriſtChrist, precious promiſespromises, that are more worth thenthan a world; and a Kingdomekingdom that ſhakesshakes not, a Crowncrown of glory that withers not, and Heavenlyheavenly treaſurestreasures that ruſtrust not. The objects of temporary grace are low, and poor, and alwayesalways within the compaſſecompass of reaſonsreason'sreasons reach.

3. True grace inablesenables a ChriſtianChristian (when he is himſelfehimself) to do ſpirituallspiritual actions with reallreal pleaſurepleasure and delight. Rom. 7. 22. eaſieeasy, and his burden is light, his commandementscommandments are not grievous, but joyous; I delight in the law of God after the inward man, ſaithsaith Paul; the bleſſedblessed man is deſcribeddescribed by this, that he delights in the law PſalPsal. 1. 2.
of the Lord; 'Tis’tis joy to the juſtjust to doedo judgment, Prov. 21. 15. ſaithsaith Solomon; To a gracious ſoulsoul all the wayesways of the Lord are pleaſantneſſepleasantness, and his paths are peace. But to ſoulssouls that have but temporary grace, but morallmoral vertuesvirtues, religious ſervicesservices, are a toiletoil, not a pleaſurepleasure; a burden, and not a delight: Wherefore have we faſtedfasted ſaysay they, IſaIsa. 58. 3. and thou ſeeſtseest not? whereforeWherefore have weewe afflicted Mal. 3. 14. our ſoulessouls, and thou takeſttakest no knowledgknowledge, &etcc. When will the new Moonemoon be gone (ſaysay thoſethose in Amos) that Amos 8. 5. we may ſellsell cornecorn? andAnd the Sabbath, that we may ſetset forth wheat, making the Epha ſmallsmall, and the ſhekellshekel great, and falſifyingfalsifying the balances by deceit.

Grace will work a mansman's heart to love, and cleave to the ſtricteſtstrictest, and ho • lieſtholiest wayesways and things of God, for their purity and ſanctitysanctity, in the face of all dangers and hardſhipshardships; Thy word is very PſalPsal. 119. 140. pure, therefore thy ſervantservant lovethlovethloueth it; others love it, and like it, and follow it, for the credit, the honour, the advantage that they get by it; but I love it for the ſpirituallspiritual beauty and purity of it. 6. True grace will inableenable a man to ſtepstep over the worldsworld's Crowncrown, to take up ChriſtsChrist's Croſſecross, to preferreprefer the croſſecross of ChriſtChrist above the glory and bravery of this world. It inabledenabled Abraham, and

When ChriſtChrist bid him goego, and ſellsell all that he had and give to the poor, &etcc. He went away ſorrowfullsorrowful, for he had great poſſeſſionspossessions. If Heavenheaven be to be had upon no other terms, ChriſtChrist may keep his Heavenheaven to himſelfehimself, hee'lhe'll have none, &etcc.

that doth conſtrainconstrain the ſoulsoul to wait onAs what I have, if offered to thee, pleaſethpleaseth not thee, oh Lord without my ſelfeself, ſoso the good things we have from thee, though they may refreſhrefresh us, yet they ſatisfiesatisfy us not without thy ſelfself. Good art thou oh Lord to the ſoulesoul that ſeeksseeks thee, what art thou then to the ſoulsoul that finds thee. God, and to act for God, and the ſenſesense of the excellency and ſweetneſssweetness of communion with God, and the choiſechoice and precious diſcoveriesdiscoveries that the ſoulesoul hath formerly had of the beauty and glory of God, whilſtwhilst it hath been in the ſerviceservice of God. The good looks, the good words, the bleſſedblessed love-letters, the glorious kiſſeskisses, and the ſweetsweet embraces that gracious ſoulessouls have had from ChriſtChrist in his ſerviceservice, do provoke and move them to waitewait upon him in holy duties; ah but reſtrainingrestraining grace, temporalltemporal grace that puts men upon religious duties, only from externallexternal motives, as the eareear of the creature, the eye of the creature, the rewards of the creature, & the keeping up of a name amongſtamongst the creatures, and a thouſandthousand ſuchsuch like conſiderationsconsiderations, as you may ſeesee in Saul, Jehu, Judas, Demas, and the Scribesscribes and PhariſeesPharisees, &etcc.

The Abbot in Melancton lived ſtrictlystrictly, and walked demurely, and look'd humbly, ſoso long as heehe was but a Monkemonk; but when by his ſeemingseeming extraordinary ſanctitysanctity, he got to be Abbot, heehe grew intollerableintolerable proud and inſolentinsolent; and being asked the reaſonreason of it, confeſſedconfessed, that his former lowly look was, but to ſeesee, if he could find the keyeskeys of the AbbieAbbeyAbby.
Such poorepoor, low, vainevain motives work temporary ſoulessouls to all the ſerviceservice they do perform, &etcc.

8. Saving grace, renewing grace wilwill cauſecause a man to follow the Lord fully in the deſertiondesertion of all ſ • insin, and in the obſervationobservation of all GodsGod's precepts. True grace works the heart to the PſalPsal. 119. 104. 128. I had rather goego to hell pure from ſinsin, thenthan to Heaven polluted with that filth, ſaithsaith AnſelmAnselm. hatred of all ſinsin, and to the love of all truth; it works a man to the hatred of thoſethose ſinssins, that for his blood he cannot conquer, and to loathloathe thoſethose ſinssins, that he would give all the world to overcome: So that a ſoulesoul truly gracious can ſaysay, though there be no one ſinnesin

My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefeſtchiefest of ten thouſandthousand. I found him whom my ſoulesoul loved, I held him and would not let him goego.

That wiſdomewisdom a Beleeverbeliever hath from ChriſtChrist, it leads him to center in the wiſdomewisdom of ChriſtChrist; and that love the ſoulesoul hath from ChriſtChrist, it leads the ſoulesoul to center in the love of ChriſtChrist; and that Righteouſneſſerighteousness the ſoulesoul hath from ChriſtChrist, it leads the ſoulesoul to reſtrest, and
center in the Righteouſneſſerighteousness of ChriſtChrist;1 Cor. 1. 30. Phil. 3. 9. 10. True grace will inableenable a ſoulesoul to ſitsit down ſatisfiedsatisfied, and contented with the naked enjoyments of ChriſtChrist. 'Tis’Tis enough, JoſephJoseph is alive. And ſoso 'tis’tis the SaintsSaints’. friends are not, &etcc. It is enough that ChriſtChrist is, that he reigns, conquers, and triumphs; ChriſtChrist is the pot of Mannahmanna, the cruicecruse of oyleoil, a bottomleſſebottomless ocean of all comfort, content, and ſatisfactionsatisfaction;
heehe that hath him wants nothing; he that wants him enjoys nothing, having nothing (ſaithsaith Paul) and yet poſſeſſingpossessing
2 Cor. 6. 10. Saint AuſtineAugustineAustin upon PſalPsal. 12. brings in God rebuking a diſcontenteddiscontented ChriſtianChristian thus; what is thy faith? have I promiſedpromised thee theſethese things? what, wert thou made a ChriſtianChristian that thou ſhouldſtshouldst flouriſhflourish here in this world? all things. I muſtmust have ChriſtChrist, and the world, or elſeelse with the young man in the Goſpelgospel (in ſoightspitesoight of my ſoulesoul) I ſhallshall forſakeforsake ChriſtChrist to follow the world. Ah! how many ſhiningshining Profeſſorsprofessors be there in the world, that cannot ſitsit down ſatisfiedsatisfied, and contented under the want of this, or that outward comfort and content, but are like Bedlams, fretting and vexing, raging, and madding, as if there were no God, no Heavenheaven, no Hellhell, nor no ChriſtChrist to make up all ſuchsuch outward wants to ſoulessouls. IAy, but a ſoulesoul truly gracious canContent is the deputy of outward felicity, & ſuppliessupplies the place where itsit's abſentabsent. As the Jews throw the book of HeſterHester to the ground before they read it, becauſebecause the name of God is not in it, as the Rabbins have obſervedobserved: So do Saints in ſomesome ſenſesense, thoſethose mercies wherein they do not read ChriſtsChrist's name, & ſeesee ChriſtsChrist's heart. Luther ſaidsaid, he had rather be in hell with ChriſtChrist, thenthan in heaven without him. ſaysay, In having nothing, I have all things, becauſebecause I have ChriſtChrist; having therefore all things in him, I ſeekseek no other reward, for heehe is the univerſalluniversal reward; ſuchsuch a ſoulesoul can ſaysay, nothing is ſweetsweet to me without the enjoyment of ChriſtChrist in it; honours, nor riches,
nor the ſmilessmiles of creatures are not ſweetsweet to me, no further thenthan I ſeesee ChriſtChrist, and taſttaste ChriſtChrist in them; the confluence of all outward good cannot make a Heavenheaven of glory in my ſoulesoul, if ChriſtChrist who is the top of my glory be abſentabsent. div.head: The Sixth Device that Satan hath to keep a poor ſoulesoul in a ſadsad, doubting, and queſtioningquestioning condition, is,
div.p: BY ſuggeſtingsuggesting to the ſoulesoul, that ſurelysurely6 Device. his eſtateestate is not good, becauſebecause he cannot joy and rejoycerejoice in ChriſtChrist, as once he could, becauſebecause he hath loſtlost that comfort and joy that once was in his ſpiritspirit. Saith Satan, thou knoweſtknowest the time was, when thy heart was much carried out to joying and rejoycingrejoicing in ChriſtChrist; thou doeſtdoest not forget the time when thy heart uſedused to be full of joy and comfort; but now, how art thou fallen in thy joyesjoys and comforts? Therefore thy eſtateestate is not good, thou doeſtdoest but deceive thy ſelfeself, to think that ever it was good, for ſurelysurely if it had, thy joy and comfort would have continued. And hereupon the ſoulesoul is apt to take part with Satan, and ſaysay, 'tis’tis even ſoso, I ſeesee all is naught, and I have but deceived my owneown ſoulesoul, &etcc.

Happily thy former joy and comfort did ſpringspring fromThe ſpiritspirit doth not every day make a feaſtfeast in the ſoulsoul, he doth not make every day to be a day of wearing the wedding robes. the witneſſewitness of the ſpiritspirit, he bearing witneſſewitness to thy ſoulesoul that thy nature was changed, thy ſinssins pardoned, thy ſoulesoul reconciled, &etcc. Now the Spirit may upon ſomesome ſpeciallspecial occaſionoccasion, bear witneſſewitness to the ſoulsoul, that the heart of God is dearly ſetset upon him, that he loves him with an everlaſtingeverlasting love, &etcc. andAnd yet the ſoulesoul may never injoyenjoy ſuchsuch a teſtimonytestimony all the dayesdays of his life again: Though the ſpiritspirit be a witneſſingwitnessing ſpiritspirit, it's not his office every day to witneſſewitness to believers their intereſtinterest in God, ChriſtChrist, Heavenheaven, &etcc.

Or happily thy former joy and comfort, did ſpringspring from the newneſſenewness and ſuddenneſſesuddenness of the change of thy condition; for a man in one hourehour to haveA pardon given unexpectedly into the hand of a malefactor, when he is on the laſtlast ſte • pstep of the ladder, ready to be turn'd off, will cauſecause muc • h joy & rejoycingrejoicing; the newneſſenewness and ſuddenneſſesuddenness of the change of his condition, will cauſecause his heart to leap and rejoycerejoice; yet in procesprocess of time much of his joy will b • e abat • ed, thothough his lif • e be as de • ar • to him ſtillstill, as ever it was. his night turn'd into day, his darkneſſedarkness turn'd into light, his bitter into ſweetsweet, GodsGod's frownesfrowns into ſmilessmiles, his hatred into love, his hell into a Heavenheaven, muſtmust greatly joy and comfort him. It cannot but make his heart to leap, and dance in him, who in one hourehour ſhallshall ſeesee Satan accuſingaccusing him, his owneown heart condemning him, the eternalleternal God frowning upon him, the gates of Heavenheaven bar'd againſtagainst him, all the creation ſtandingstanding armed at the leaſtleast beck of God, to execute vengeance on him, and the mouth of the infernallinfernal pit open to receive him. Now in this hour, for ChriſtChrist to come to the amazed ſoulesoul, and ſaysay to it, I have trod the Wine • -preſſepress of my FathersFather's wrath for thee, I have laid down my life a ranſomeransom for thee, by my blood I have ſatisfiedsatisfied my FathersFather's Juſticejustice, and pacified his anger, and procured his love for thee; by my blood I have purchaſedpurchased the pardon of thy ſinssins, thy freedom from hell, and thy right to Heavenheaven, &etcc. Oh! how wonderfully will this cauſecause the ſoulesoul to leap for joy?

The fifth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice5 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, to conſiderconsider, that God will
reſtorerestore and make up the comforts of his people; though thy candle be put out, HudſonHudson the Martyr deſerteddeserted at the ſtakestake, went from under his chain, and having prayed earneſtlyearnestly, was comforted immediately, and ſufferedsuffered valiantly. So Mr. Glover, when he was within ſightsight of the ſtakestake, cryedcried out to his friend, he is come, he is come, meaning the comforter that ChriſtChrist promiſedpromised to ſendsend. yet God will light it againeagain, and make it burn more light thenthan ever; though thy ſunsun for the preſentpresent be clouded, yet he that rides upon the clouds, ſhallshall ſcatterscatter thoſethose clouds, and cauſecause the ſunsun to ſhineshine, and warm thy heart, as in forme • r dayesdays, as the PſalmiſtPsalmist ſpeakesspeaks, PſPs. 71. 20, 21. Thou which haſthast ſhewedshowed me great and ſo • resore troubles, ſhaltshalt quicken me againeagain, and ſhaltshalt bring me up againeagain from the depths of the earth. Thou ſhaltshalt increaſeincrease my greatneſſegreatness, and comfort me on every ſideside. God takes away a little comfort, that he may make room in the ſoulesoul for a greater degree of comfort. This the Prophetprophet IſaiahIsaiah ſweetlysweetly ſhewesshows, IſaIsa. 57. 18. I have ſeenseen his wayesways, and will healeheal him, I will lead him alſoalso, and reſto • rerestore comforts unto him, and to his mourners. Bear up ſweetlysweetly oh precious ſoulesoul! thyThy ſtormestorm ſhallshall end in a calm; and thy dark night in a ſunsun-ſhineshine day; thy mourning ſhallshall be turn'd into rejoycingrejoicing, and the waters of conſolationconsolation ſhallshall be ſweetersweeter and higher in thy ſoulesoul, thenthanSee alſoalso the 126 PſalPsal. 6. v. and the 42 PſalPsal. 7, 8. ever; the me • rcy is ſurelysurely thine, but the time of giving it is the LordsLord's: wait but a litt • le, and thou ſhaltshalt find the Lord comforting thee on every ſideside.

div.head: The ſeventhseventh Device that Satan hath to keep ſoulssouls in a doubting and queſtioningquestioning condition, is,
div.p: BY ſuggeſtingsuggesting to the ſoulesoul his often7 Device. relapſesrelapses into the ſamesame ſinsin which formerly he hath purſuedpursued with particular sorrow, grief, ſhameshame and tears, and prayed, complained, and reſolvedresolved againſtagainst. Saith Satan, thy heart is not right with God, ſurelysurely thy eſtateestate is not good, thou doſtdost but flatter thy ſelfeself, to think that ever God will eternally owneown, and embrace ſuchsuch a one as thou art, who complaineſtcomplainest againſtagainst ſinsin, and yet relapſeſtrelapsest into the ſamesame ſinsin, who with tearestears and groanesgroans confeſſeſtconfessest thy ſinsin, and yet ever and anon art fallen into the ſamesame ſinsin, &etcc.

I confeſſeconfess this is a very ſadsad condition for a ſoulesoul, after he hath obtained mercy and pity from the Lord, after God hath ſpokenspoken peace and pardon to him, and wip't the tears from his eyes, and ſetset him upon his legs, to returnereturn to folly; ah! how doedo relapſesrelapses lay men open
to the greateſtgreatest afflictions, and worſtworstA backſliderbackslider may ſaysay (opera & impenſaimpensa periit) all my painespains and charge is loſtlost. temptations? How doedo they make the wound to bleed afreſhafresh? How doedo they darken and cloud former aſſurancesassurances and evidences • for Heavenheaven? How doedo they put a ſwordsword into the hand of conſcienceconscience to cut and ſlaſhslash the ſoulesoul? They raiſeraise ſuchsuch fearesfears, terroursterrors, horrourshorrors, and doubts in the ſoulesoul, that the ſoulesoul cannot be ſoso frequent in duty, as formerly, nor ſoso fervent in duty as formerly, nor ſoso confident in duty as formerly, nor ſoso bold, familiar, and delightfulldelightful with God in duty as formerly; nor ſoso conſtantconstant in duty as formerly: they give Satan an advantage to triumph over ChriſtChrist; they make the work of repentance mor • e difficult; they make a mansman's life a burden, and they render death to be very terrible unto the ſoulesoul, &etcc.

div.head: Now the Remedies againſtagainst this device of Satan are theſethese that follow.
div.p:
THeThe firſtfirst Remedieremedy againſtagainst this device1 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that there are many Scriptures that doedo clearly evidence a poſſibilitypossibility of the StSt. fallingFallingsaints falling into the ſamesame ſinssins, whereof they have formerly repented. HoſHos. 14. 4. I will healeheal their backsliding, I will love them freely, for mine anger is turned away from them, ſaithsaith the Lord by the Prophetprophet HoſeaHosea, ſoso the Prophetprophet Jeremiah ſpeaksspeaks, IerJer. 3. 12. 14. GoeGo and proclaimeproclaim theſethese words towards the North▪, and ſaysay, returnereturn thou back-ſlidingsliding IſraelIsrael▪, ſaithsaith the Lord, and I will not cauſecause mine anger to fall upon you: for I am mercifullmerciful▪, ſaithsaith the The ſinsin of backſlidingbacksliding is a ſoulsoul-wounding ſinsin. I will healeheal their backſlidingbacksliding: you read of no arms for the back, though you doedo for the breaſtbreast. Lord, and I will not keep anger for ever. TurneTurn, oh backsliding IſraelIsrael, ſaithsaith the Lord, for I am married unto you: And I will take you one of a Citycity, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion: So the PſalmiſtPsalmist, They turned back and dealt unfaithfully like their Fathers, they were turned aſideaside like a deceitfulldeceitful bow. And no wonder, for thothough their repentance be never ſoso ſinceresincere and ſoundsound, yet their graces are but weak,
and their mortification imperfect inWhen a ſouldiersoldier bragged too much of a great ſcarscar in his forehead, AuguſtusAugustus CaeſarCaesar (in whoſewhose time ChriſtChrist was borneborn) asked him if he did not get it when he looked back as he fled. this life; though by grace they are freed from the dominion of ſinsin, and from the damnatory power of every ſinsin, and from the love of all ſinsin, yet grace doth not free them from the ſeedseed of any one ſinsin; and therefore 'tis’tis poſſiblepossible for a ſoulesoul to fall againeagain and againeagain into the ſamesame ſinsin; if the fire be not wholly put out, who would thinkethink it impoſſibleimpossible that it ſhouldshould catch and burneburn againeagain and againeagain?

The ſecondsecond Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice2 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider, that God hath no where ingagedengaged himſelfehimself by any particular promiſepromise, that ſoulessouls converted and united to ChriſtChrist, ſhallshall not fall againeagain and againeagain into the ſamesame ſinssins after converſionconversion. I cannot find in the whole Book of God, where heIn ſomesome caſescases the Saints have found God better thenthan his word; he promi • ſedpromised the Children of IſraelIsrael onelyonly the Land of Canaan, but beſidesbesides that he gave them two other KingdomesKingdoms, which he never promiſedpromised. And to Zachary he promiſedpromised to give him his ſpeechspeech at the birth of the child, but beſidesbesides that, he gave him the gift of Prophecy. hath promiſedpromised any ſuchsuch ſtrengthstrength or power againſtagainst this or that particular ſinsin, as that the ſoulesoul ſhallshall be for ever (in this life) put out of a poſſibilitypossibility of falling againeagain and againeagain into the ſamesame ſinssins; and where God hath not a mouth to ſp • eakspeak, I muſtmust not have a heart to believe. God will graciouſlygraciously pardon thoſethose ſinssins to his people, that he will not in this life effectually ſubduesubdue in his people. I would goego far to ſpeakspeak with that ſoulesoul that can ſhewshow a promiſepromise, that when our
ſorrowsorrow and grief hath been ſoso great, or ſoso much, for this or that ſinsin, that then God will preſervepreserve us from ever falling into the ſamesame ſinsin; the ſightsight of ſuchsuch a promiſepromise would be as life from the dead, to many a precious ſoulesoul, who deſiresdesires nothing more thenthan to keepekeep cloſeclose to ChriſtChrist, and fearesfears nothing more thenthan backſlidingbacksliding from ChriſtChrist.

The third Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice3 Remedy. of Satan, is ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider, that the moſtmost renowned, and now crowned Saintssaints, have in the dayesdays of their being on earth, relapſedrelapsed into one and theA ſheepsheep may often ſlipslip into a ſloughslough, as well as a ſwineswine. ſamesame ſinsin. Lot was twice overcome with wine; John twice worſhippedworshipped the Angelangel; Abraham did often diſſembledissemble, and IaylayJay his wife open to adultery, to ſavesave his owneown life, which ſomesome Heathensheathens would not have done. And it came to Gen. 20. 13. c • h. 12. paſſepass, when God cauſedcaused me to wander from my FathersFather's houſehouse, that I ſaidsaid unto her, this is thy kindneſſekindness which thou ſhaltshalt ſhewshow unto me, at every place whetherwhither we ſhallshall come, ſaysay of me, he is my brother. David in hisPerhaps the ProdigallProdigal ſetssets out unto us, a ChriſtianChristian relapſtrelapsed; for he was a ſonson before, and with his Father, & then went away from him and ſpentspent all, and yet he was not quite undone, but returned againeagain. wrath was reſolvedresolved, if ever man was, that he would be the death of Nabal, and all his innocent Familyfamily, and after this he fell into the foulefoul murthermurder of ƲriahUriah. Though ChriſtChrist told his Diſciplesdisciples that his Kingdomekingdom was not of this world, yet againeagain, and againeagain, and again, three
ſeverallseveral times, they would needs be on horſehorse-back, they would fainefain be high, great, and glorious in this world; their pride and ambitious humour put them (that were but as ſoso many baggarsbeggars) upon ſtrivingstriving for preheminencepreeminence, and greatneſſegreatness in the world, when their Lord and Maſtermaster told them 3 ſeverallseveral times of his ſufferingssufferings in the world, and of his going out of the world. JehoſhaphatJehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 18. ch. 1. 2. 3. 30, 31. though a godly man, yet joynesjoins affinity with wicked Ahab, and though he was ſavedsaved by a miracle, yet ſoonsoon after he falsfalls into the ſamesame ſinsin, and joynesjoins himſelfhimself with ch. 20. 35. 36, 37. Ahaziah, King of IſraelIsrael, who did very wickedly. SampſonSamson is • by the Spirit of the Lord numbrednumbered among the faithful worthies,Heb. 11. 32. and yet he fell often into one groſsgross ſinsin, as is evident in the book of Judges; Jud. 14. 15. 16. ch. Peter you know relapſtrelapsed often, and ſoso did Jonah; and this comes to paſſepass, that they may ſeesee their owneown inability to ſtandstand, to reſiſtresist, or overcome any temptation, or corruption. And that they may be taken off from all falſefalse confidences, and reſtrest wholywholly upon God, and onelyonly upon God, and alwayesalways upon God; and for the praiſepraise and honour of the power, wiſdomewisdom, skill, mercy, andThe Prodigal ſawsaw the compaſſioncompassion of his Father, the greater in receiving him, after he had run away from him. goodneſſegoodness of the Phyſitianphysician of our ſoulssouls, that can healeheal, help, and cure, when the diſeaſedisease is moſtmost dangerous, when the
ſoulesoul is relapſtrelapsed, and growesgrows worſeworse and worſeworse, and when others ſaysay there is no help for him in his God, and when his owneown heart and hopes are dying.

The fourth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice4 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, to conſiderconsider, that there • are relapſesrelapses into enormities, and there are relapſesrelapses into infirmities; now 'tis’tis not uſuallusual with God to leave his peopleRelapſesRelapses into enormities are (peccata vulnerantia & diviſtantiadevastantiadivistantia) wounding & waſtingwasting ſinssins. Therefore the Lord is graciouſlygraciously pleaſedpleased to put under his everlaſtingeverlasting arms, and ſtaystay his choſenchosen ones from frequent falling into them. frequently to relapſerelapse into enormities, for by his ſpiritspirit and grace, by his ſmilessmiles and frownesfrowns, by his word and rod, he doth uſuallyusually preſervepreserve his people from a frequent relapſingrelapsing into enormities; yet he doth leave his choiceſtchoicest ones frequently to relapſerelapse into infirmities (and of his grace he pardons them in courſecourse) as idle words, paſſionpassion, vainevain thoughts, &etcc. Though gracious ſoulessouls ſtrivestrive againſtagainst theſethese, and complainecomplain of theſethese, and weep over theſethese, yet the Lord to keep them humble, leaves them frequently to relapſerelapse into theſethese; and theſethese frequent relapſesrelapses into infirmities ſhallshall never be their bane, becauſebecause they be their burdenburden.

The fiftfifth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice5 Remedy. of Satan, is to conſiderconsider, that there areThere is a great difference betwenbetween a ſheepsheep that by weakneſſeweakness falsfalls into the mire, & a ſwineswine, that delights to wallow in the mire; between a woman that is forced, though ſheshe ſtrivesstrives, and cries out, and and an alluring adultreſsadulteressadultress. involuntary relapſesrelapses, and there are voluntary relapſesrelapses; involuntary relapſesrelapses are, when the reſolutionresolution and full bent of the heart is againſtagainst ſinsin, when the ſoulsoul ſtrivesstrives with all its might againſtagainst ſinsin, by
ſighessighs and groans, by prayers and tears, and yet out of weakneſſeweakness, is forced to fall back into ſinsin, becauſebecause there is not ſpirituallspiritual ſtrengthstrength enough to overcome; Now though involuntary relapſesrelapses muſtmust humble us, yet they muſtmust never diſcouragediscourage, nor deject us, for God will freely and readily pardon thoſethose in courſecourse. Voluntary relapſesrelapses are, when the ſoulesoul longs, and loves to return to the fleſhflesh-pots of Egypt; when 'tis’tis a pleaſurepleasure, and a paſtimepastime to a man to return to his old courſescourses; ſuchsuch voluntary relapſesrelapses ſpeakspeak out the man blinded, hardnedhardened, and ripened for rulneruin, &etcc.

The ſixthsixth Remedieremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice 6 Remedy. of SathanSatan, is, to conſiderconsider, that there is no ſuchsuch power, or infinite vertuevirtue in theChriſtChrist upbradedupbraided his DiſciplesDisciples for their unbelief, and hardneſſehardness of heart, who had ſeeneseen his glory, as the glory of the only begotten ſonson of God, full of grace and truth.. John 1 John. 14. greateſtgreatest horror, or ſorrowsorrow the ſoulsoul can be under for ſinsin, nor in the ſweeteſtsweetest, or choſeſtchoicestchosest diſcoveriesdiscoveries of GodsGod's grace, and love to the ſoulesoul; as for ever to fence, and ſecuresecure the ſoulesoul from relapſingrelapsing into the ſamesame ſinsin; Gracegrace is but a created habitehabit, that may be prevailed againſtagainst by the ſecretsecret, ſubtilesubtlesubtile, and ſtrongstrong workings of ſinsin in our hearts: And thoſethose diſcoveriesdiscoveries that God makes of his love, beauty, and glory to the ſoulesoul, doedo not always abide in their freſhneſſefreshness, and power upon the heart; but by degrees they fade, and wearewear off, and then the ſoulesoul
may return again to folly; As we ſeesee in Peter, who after he had a glorious teſtimonytestimonyMat. 16. 15, 16, 17, 18, 19. 22, 23, 24. from ChriſtChrist his own mouth, of his bleſſedneſſeblessedness and happineſſehappiness, labours to prevent ChriſtChrist from going up to JeruſalemJerusalem to ſuffersuffer out of baſebase ſlaviſhslavish fears, that he and his fellows could not be ſecuresecure, if his Maſtermaster ſhouldshould be brought to ſuffersuffer. And againeagain, after this, ChriſtChrist had him up into the Mount, and thereMat. 717. 1, 2, 3. ſhewedshowed him his beauty, and glory, to ſtrengthenstrengthen him againſtagainst the hour of tentation that was a commingcoming upon him; and yet ſoonesoon after he had the honour, and happineſſehappiness of ſeeingseeing the glory of the Lord (which moſtmost of the Diſciplesdisciples had not) he baſelybasely, and moſtmost ſhamefullyshamefully denies the Lord of glory, thinkingMat. 26. 69. ult. by that means to provide for his owneown ſafetysafety: And yet again, after ChriſtChrist had broke his heart with a lookelook of love, for his moſtmost unlovely dealings, and bade them that were firſtfirst acquainted with his reſurrectionresurrection, to goego and tell Peter that he was riſenrisen; I ſaysay, after all this, ſlaviſhslavish fears prevail upon him, and he baſelybasely diſſemblesdissembles, and plays ehethe IewJew with the IewesJews, and the Gentile with the Gentiles, to the ſeducingseducing of Barnabas, GalGal. 2. 11, 12, 13. &etcc.

Yet by way of caution, know it's very rare, that God doth leave his beloved
ones frequently, to relapſerelapse into one and the ſamesame groſſegross ſinsin; for the law of nature is in armesarms againſtagainst groſſegross ſinssins, aſwellas well as the law of grace; ſoso that a gracious ſoulesoul cannot, dares not, will not frequently returnereturn to groſſegross folly. And God hath made even his deareſtdearest ones dearly ſmartsmart for their relapſesrelapses, as may be ſeenseen by his dealings with SamſonSamson, IehoſaphatJehoshaphatJehosaphat, and Peter; Ah Lord! whatWhat a hard heart hath that man, that can ſeesee thee ſtrippingstripping and whipping thy deareſtdearest ones for their relapſesrelapses, and yet make nothing of returning to folly, &etcc.

div.head: The eighth Device that Satan8 Device. hath to keepekeep ſoulessouls in a doubting, and questioning condition, is,
div.p:
BY perſwadingpersuading them that theistheir eſtateestate is not good, their hearts are not upright, their graces are not ſoundsound, be • cauſebecause they are ſoso followed, vexed, and tormented with 'temptationstemptations; 'tis’tis his method, firſtfirst to vex, and weary the ſoulsoul with temptations, and then to tempt
the ſoulesoul, that ſurelysurely 'tis’tis not beloved,He may ſoso tempt, as to make a Saint weary of his life. Job 10. 1. My ſoulesoul is weary of my life. becauſebecause 'tis’tis ſoso much tempted; and by this ſtratagemstratagem he keeps many precious ſoulssouls in a ſadsad, doubting, and mourning temper many years, as many of the precious ſonnessons of Sion have found by wofullwoefulwoful experience, &etcc.

div.head: Now the remedies againſtagainst this Device of Satan are theſethese that follow.
div.p:
THeThe firſtfirst Remedieremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice 1 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that thoſethose that have been beſtbest, and moſtmost beloved, have been moſtmost tempted by Satan. Though Satan can never rob a ChriſtianChristian of his Crowncrown, yet ſuchsuch is his malice, that heehe will therefore tempt, that he may ſpoylespoil them of their comforts; ſuchsuch is his enmity to the Father, that the nearer and dearer any child is to him, the more will Satan trouble him, and vex him with temptations;PiratsPirates do not uſeuse to ſetset upon poor, empty veſſelsvessels; and beggars need not fearefear the thieſethiefthiese; thoſethose that have moſtmost of God, and moſtmost rich in grace, ſhallshall be moſtmost ſetset upon by Satan, who is the greateſtgreatest and wiſeſtwisest Pirate in the world. ChriſtChrist himſelfehimself was moſtmost neernear, and moſtmost dearedear, moſtmost innocent, and moſtmost excellent, and yet none ſoso much tempted as ChriſtChrist; David was dearly beloved, and yet by Satan tempted to number the people; IobJob was highly praiſedpraised by God
himſelfehimself, and yet much tempted, witneſſewitness thoſethose ſadsad things that fell from his mouth, when he was wet to the skin; Peter was much prized by ChriſtChrist, witneſſewitness that choiſechoice teſtimonytestimony that ChriſtChrist gave of his faith and happineſſehappiness, and his ſhewingshowing him his glory in the Mount, and that eye of pity that he caſtcast upon him after his fearfullfearful fall, &etcc. andAnd yet tempted by Satan. And the Lord ſaidsaid, Luke 22. 31, 32. Simon, Simon, behold Satan hath deſireddesired to have you, that he may ſiftsift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith failefail thee not, &etcc.

Paul had the honour of being exalted as high as high as heaven, and of ſeeingseeing that glory that could not be expreſtexpressed; and yet heehe was no ſoonersooner ſteptstepped out of Heavenheaven, but he is buffettedbuffeted by Satan, leſtlest he ſhouldshould be exalted above meaſuremeasure. The fifth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice5 Remedy. of Satan, is, to dwell much upon the famous examples of thoſethose worthy Saintssaints that have denyeddenied themſelvesthemselves, and prefer'd the publickpublic good before their owneown particular advantage: As MoſesMoses; And the Lord ſaidsaid unto MoſesMoses, let me alone that I may deſtroyedestroy them, and blot out their name from under Heavenheaven, and I will make of thee a Nationnation might •• termightier, and greater thenthan they; oh! but this offer would not'Tis’Tis’tis good to be of his opinion & mind, who was rather willing to beautifiebeautify Italy thenthan his own houſehouse. take with MoſesMoses, he being a man of a brave publiquepublic ſpiritspirit, is hot in his deſiresdesires and prayers that the people might be ſparedspared and pardoned; ſaithsaith he, pardon I beſeechbeseech thee the iniquity of this people, according unto the greatneſſegreatness of thy mercy, and as thou haſthast forgiven this people from Egypt untilluntil now. And the Lord ſaidsaid, I have pardoned according to thy word. Ah! ſ ••• houldAh! should God make ſuchsuch an offer to many that write themſelvesthemselves MoſesMoses, and are called
by many, MoſesMoses, I am afraid they would prefer their own advantage above theThe AntientsAncients were wont to place the Statues of their Princes by their fountains, intimating they were (or at leaſtleast ſhouldshould be) fountains of the publickpublic good. publiquepublic good; they would not care what become of the people, ſoso they and theirs might be made great and glorious in the world; they would not care ſoso they might have a BabellBabel built for them, though it was upon the aſhesashes, and ruineruin of the people; baſerbaser ſpiritsspirits thenthan theſethese are not in hell, no, not in hell, and I am ſuresure there are no ſuchsuch ſpiritsspirits in Heavenheaven; ſuchsuch mensmen's hearts and principles muſtmust be chang'd, or they wilwill be undone for ever. Nehemiah was aA certainecertain great EmperourEmperor coming into Egypt, to ſhewshow the zeal he had for the publickpublic good, ſaithsaith to the Aegyptians, draw from me as from your river Nilus. choice ſoulesoul, a man of a brave publickpublic ſpiritspirit, a man that ſpentspent his time, his ſtrengthstrength, and his eſtateestate for the good and eaſeease of his people. Moreover (ſaithsaith he) from the time that I was appointed to be their GovernourGovernor in the Landland of Judah, from the twentieth yeeryear, even unto the two and thirtieth yeareyear of Artaxerxes the King, that is, twelve yearesyears; I and my brethren have not eaten the bread of the GovernourGovernor. Yea, alſoalso I continued in the workework of this wall, neither bought we any land, and all my ſervantsservants were gathered thither unto the workework. Moreover, there were at my table an hundred and fifty of the JewesJews and Rulersrulers, beſidesbesides thoſethose that came unto us from among the Heathenheathen that are about us. Now that which was prepared for me daily, was
one OxeOx, and ſixesix choice ſheepsheep: alſoalso fowlesfowls were prepared for me, and once in ten dayesdays ſtorestore of all ſortssorts of wine; yet for all this required not I the bread of the GovernourGovernor, becauſebecause the bondage was heavy upon the people. ThinkeThink upon me, my God, for good, according to all that I have done for this people. So Daniel was a man of a brave publickpublic ſpiritspirit; Then the Preſidentspresidents and Princesprinces The CounſellorCounsellor ſaithsaith a StateſStates-man ſhouldshould be thus tripartited, his will to God, his love to his MaſterMaster, his heart to his CountreyCountry, his ſecretsecret to his friend, his time to buſiſineſſebusinessbusisiness. ſoughtsought to findefind occaſionoccasion againſtagainst Daniel, concerning the Kingdomekingdom, but they could findefind no occaſionoccasion nor fault, for as much as he was faithfullfaithful, neither was there any errourerror, or fault found in him. Then ſaidsaid theſethese men, we ſhallshall not findefind any occaſionoccasion againſtagainst this Daniel, except we findefind it againſtagainst him, concerning the law of his God.

ChriſtChrist had a publickpublic ſpiritspirit, heehe laid out himſelfehimself, and laid down himſelfehimself for a publickpublic good. Oh! never leave looking and meditating upon theſethese precious and ſweetsweet examples, till your ſoulessouls are quicknedquickened, and raiſedraised up, to act for the publickpublic good, more thenthan for your owneown particular advantage; many SolomonsSolomon's TribunallTribunal was underpropt with Lions, to ſhewshow what ſpiritspirit, and mettallmettle a MagiſtrateMagistrate ſhouldshould be made of. Heathensheathens have been excellent at this. Macrobius writes of AuguſtusAugustus CaeſarCaesar (in whoſewhose time ChriſtChrist was borneborn) that heehe carried ſuchsuch an entire and fatherly affection to the Commoncommon-wealth, that he called it (filiam ſuamsuam) his own daughter, and therefore refuſedrefused to be called
(Dominus) the Lord or Maſtermaster of his Countreycountry, and would only be called (pater patriae) Father of his Countreycountry, becauſebecause he governed it not by fearefear (per timorem ſedsed per amorem) but by love; the Senatesenate and the people of Rome joyntlyjointly ſalutingsaluting him, by the name of (pater patriae) Father of his Countreycountry. The people very much lamented his death, uſingusing that ſpeechspeech, Would heehe had
ƲtinamUtinam aut non naſcereturnasceretur, aut non moreretur. never been borneborn, or never dyeddied. So Marcus Regulus, to ſavesave his Countreycountry from ruineruin, expoſedexposed himſelfehimself to the greateſtgreatest ſufferingssufferings that the malice and rage of his Enemiesenemies could inflict. So Titus and AriſtidesAristides, and many others have been famous for their preferring the publickpublic good above their own advantage. My prayer is, and ſhallshall be, that all our Rulersrulers may be ſoso ſpiritedspirited by God, that they may be willing to be any thing, to be nothing, to deny themſelvesthemselves, and to trample their ſinfullsinful ſelvesselves under feet, in order to the honour of God, and a publickpublic good, that ſoso neither Saintssaints nor Heathensheathens may be witneſſeswitnesses againſtagainst them in that day, wherein the hearts & practiſespractises of all the Rulersrulers in the world ſhallshall be open, and bare before him that ſhallshall judge the world in Righteouſneſsrighteousness, and Judgmentjudgment, &etcc.

The ſixthsixth Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice6 RemedieRemedy.
of Satan, is, ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider, that ſelfself is a great let to divine things, therefore the Prophetsprophets and Apoſtlesapostles were uſuallyusually carried out of themſelvesthemselves, when they had the cleareſtclearest, choiſeſtchoicest, higheſthighest, and moſtmost glorious viſionsvisions. Self-ſeekingseeking blinds the ſoulsoul, that it cannot ſeesee a beauty in ChriſtChrist, nor an excellency in holineſsholiness; it diſtempersdistempers the palate, that a man cannot taſtetaste ſweetneſſesweetness in the word of God, nor in the ways of God, nor in the ſocietysociety of the people of God; it ſhutsshuts the hand againſtagainst all the ſoulesoul-enriching offers of ChriſtChrist; it hardens the heart aganſtagainstaganst all the knocks and entreaties of ChriſtChrist; it makes the ſoulsoul as an empty vine, and as a barren wilderneſſewilderness. IſraelIsrael is an empty HoſeaHosea 10. 1. vine, he brings forth fruit to himſelfhimself. There is nothing that ſpeaksspeaks a man to be more empty, and void of God, ChriſtChrist, and grace, thenthan ſelfself-ſeekingseeking. The PhariſeesPharisees SelfeSelf-ſeek • ersseekers with EſauEsau, prefer a meſſemess of pottage above thairtheir birth-right, and with the men of Shechem, eſteemesteem the bramble above the Vine, the Olive, and the figtree, yea empty things above a full ChriſtChrist▪, & baſebase things above a glorious ChriſtChrist. were great ſelfself-ſeekersseekers, & great undervaluers of ChriſtChrist his word & ſpiritspirit. There is not a greater hindrance to all the duties of piety, thenthan ſelfself-ſeekingseeking; oh! this is that that keeps many a ſoulesoul from looking after God, and the precious things of eternity; they cannot waitewait on GOD, nor act for God, nor abide in thoſethose ways wherein they might meetemeet with God, by reaſonreason of ſelfeself; ſelfself-ſeekingseeking is that which puts many a
man upon neglecting, and ſlightingslighting the things of his peace; ſelfself-ſeekersseekers will neither go into Heavenheaven themſelvesthemselves, nor ſuffersuffer others to enter, that are ready to take the Kingdomekingdom by violence, as you may ſeesee in the Scribesscribes and PhariſeesPharisees. Oh! but a gracious ſpiritspirit is acted quite otherwayesotherwise, as you may ſeesee in that ſweetsweet Scripture, Cant. 7. 13. At our gates are all manner of pleaſantpleasant fruits, new Cant. 7. 13. and old, which I have laid up for thee oh my beloved. All the Churchchurch hath and is, isThe SaintsSaints’ Motto is, Propter te, Domine, propter te. only for him; let others bearebear fruit to themſelvesthemselves, and lay up for themſelvesthemselves; gracious ſpiritsspirits will hide for ChriſtChrist, and lay up for ChriſtChrist; all the divine indeavoursendeavours, and productions of Saintssaints fall into GodsGod's boſomebosom, and empty themſelvesthemselves into his lap. As ChriſtChrist layeslays up his merits for them, his graces for them, his comforts for them, his Crowncrown for them: ſoso they lay up all their fruits, and all their loves, all their graces, andThe SaintsSaints’ Motto is, non nobis Domine. all their experience, and all their ſervicesservices, only for him, who is the ſoulesoul of their comforts, and the crown, and top of all their royalty, and glory, &etcc.

div.head: The ſecondsecond Device that Satan2 Device. hath to enſnareensnare, and deſtroydestroy the great and honourable of the earth, is,
div.p:
BY engaging them againſtagainst the people of the moſtmost high, againſtagainst thoſethose that are his jewels, his pleaſantpleasant portion, the delight of his eye, and the joy of his heart, &etcc. Thus he drew Pharaoh to engageExod. 14. againſtagainst the children of IſraelIsrael, and that was his overthrow. So he engagedHeſterHester 7. Haman againſtagainst the IewsJews, and ſoso brought him to hang upon that gallows that he had made for Mordecai. So he engagedDan. 6. thoſethose Princesprinces and Preſidentspresidents againſtagainst Daniel, which was the utter ruineruin of them and their relations. So in Revel. 20.Revel. 20. 7, 8, 9. 7, 8, 9. And when the thouſandthousand yearesyears are expired, Satan ſhallshall be looſedloosed out of his priſonprison. And he ſhallshall goego out to deceive the Nationsnations which are in the four quarters of the earth▪, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battle: whoſewhose number is as the ſandsand of the Sea. And they went up upon the breadth of the earth, and compaſſedcompassed the camp of the Saintssaints about, and the beloved Citycity:
and fire came down from God out of Heavenheaven, and conſumedconsumed them.

div.head: Now the Remedies againſtagainst this device of Satan are theſethese that follow.
div.p:

Saintssaints, but have been ruin'd by the God of Saintssaints; divine juſticejustice hath been too hard for all that have oppoſedopposed and engaged againſtagainst the Saintssaints, as is evident in Saul, Pharaoh, Haman, &etcc. He reproved Kings for their ſakessakes, ſayingsaying, Touch not mine anointed, nor do my Prophetsprophets no harm; when men of BalaamsBalaam's ſpiritspirit tndand principles have been engaged againſtagainst the Saintssaints, how hath the Angelangel of the Lord met them in the way, and juſledjostledjusled their bones againſtagainst the wall? howHow hath heehe broke their backs, and necks, and by his drawn ſwordsword cut them off in the prime of their dayesdays, and in the height of their ſinssins? blood as water upon the ground? howHow hath he laid their honour and glory in the duſtdust? whoWho in the pride, and madneſſemadness of their hearts ſaidsaid, as Pharaoh, we will purſuepursue, we will overtake, we will divide the ſpoilespoil, our luſtslusts ſhallshall be ſatisfiedsatisfied upon them: we will draw our ſwordsword, our hand ſhallshall deſtroydestroy them; in the things wherein they have ſpokenspoken & done proudly, Juſticejustice hath been above them. HiſtoryHistory abounds in nothing more thenthan in inſtancesinstances of this kind, &etcc.
