The 3. RemedieRemedy againſtagainst this device of3 RemedieRemedy. Satan, is, to conſiderconsider, that you cannot engage againſtagainst the Saintssaints, but you muſtmust Acts 5. 39. It ſeemsseems to be drawn from the ſablefablesable of the GyantsGiants, which were ſaidsaid to make War with the Gods. engage againſtagainst God himſelfehimself, by reaſonreason of that neernear, and bleſſedblessed union that is between God and them; you cannot be fighters againſtagainst the Saintssaints, but you will be found in the caſtingcasting up of the account, to be fighters againſtagainst God himſelfhimself; and what greater madneſſemadness, thenthan for weakneſſeweakness it ſelfeself to engage againſtagainst an almighty ſtrengthstrength; the neernear union that is between the Lord and Beleeversbelievers, is ſetset forth by that neernear union that is betwixt a husband and his Wifewife.The ſoulessoul'ssouls happineſſehappiness conſiſtsconsists not in any thing but in its union with God; nor its miſerymisery lies not ſoso much in any thing, as in its diſuniondisunion from God. (They two ſhallshall be one fleſhflesh; This is a great MiſteryMysteryMistery, but I ſpeakespeak concerning ChriſtChrist & the Churchchurch) We are members of his body, of his fleſhflesh, and of his bones, ſaithsaith the Apoſtleapostle: This neernear union is ſetset forth by that union that is between the head and the members, which make up one body, and by that union that is betwixt the graft and the ſtockstock, which are made one by inſcitionincisioninscition. The union between the Lord and a Beleeverbeliever is ſoso neernear, that you cannot ſtrikestrike a Beleeverbeliever, but the Lord is ſenſiblesensible of it, and takes it as done to himſelfhimself, Saul, Saul, why perſecuteſtpersecutest thou Acts 9. 4. IſaIsa. 63. 9. me? And in all their afflictions he was afflicted, &etcc. Ah ſoulessouls! whoWho ever engaged againſtagainst God, and proſperedprospered? whoWho
ever took up the ſwordsword againſtagainst him, but periſhtperisht by it? God can ſpeakspeak you to hell, and nod you to hell at pleaſurepleasure; 'tis’tis your greateſtgreatest concernment to lay downedown your weapons at his feet, and to PſalPsal. 2. 12. kiſſekiss the ſonneson leſtlest he be angry, and you periſhperish in the mid-way.

The 4th Remedieremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice 4 RemedieRemedy. of Satan is, ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that Hic homo potuit apud Deum quod voluit. Said one concerning Luther, he could have what heehe would of God. you are much engaged to the Saintssaints (as inſtrumentsinstruments) for the mercies that you do enjoy, and for the preventing and removing of many a judgment, that otherwiſeotherwise might have been your ruineruin, before this day; were it not for the Saintssaints’saints ſakesake, God would quickly make the Heavensheavens to be as braſſebrass, and the Earthearth as iron, God would quickly ſtripstrip thee of thy Robesrobes, and glory, and ſetset thee upon the dunghill with Job: They are the props that bear the world from falling about thy earesears, and that keep the iron rod from breaking of thy bones. Therefore he ſaidsaid that heehe would PſalPsal. 106. 23. deſtroydestroy them, had not MoſesMoses his choſenchosen ſtoodstood before him in the breach, to turn away Prayer is (porta coeli, clavis ParadiſiParadisi) the gate of Heaven, a key to let us into ParadiſeParadise. his wrath, leſtlest he ſhouldshould deſtroydestroy them.

Ah! had not the Saintssaints many a time caſtcast themſelvesthemselves into the breach, betwixt GodsGod's wrath and you, you had been cut off from the land of the living, and have had your portion with thoſethose,
whoſewhose names are written in the duſtdust;When the danger is over the Saint is forgotten, is a French Proverb, and that which many Saints in England have found by experience. many a Nationnation, many a Citycity, and many a Familyfamily is ſurroundedsurrounded with bleſſingsblessings for the JoſephsJosephs’Josephs ſakessakes that live therein, and are preſervedpreserved from many calamities and miſeriesmiseries, for the MoſesesMoseses, the Daniels, the Noahs, and the JobsJobs’ ſakessakes, that dwell amongſtamongst them. THeThe firſtfirst Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice1 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, to dwell more upon one anothersanother's graces, thenthan upon one anothersanother's weakneſſesweaknesses and infirmities: 'tis’tis ſadsad to conſiderconsider, that Saintssaints ſhouldshould have Flavius VeſpaſianusVespasianus (the EmperourEmperor) was more ready to conceal the vices of his friends, thenthan their virtues; can you think ſeriouſlyseriously of this ChriſtiansChristians (that a Heathen ſhouldshould excellexcel you) & not bluſhblush? 2 Cor. 2. 7, 8. many eyes to behold one anothersanother's infirmities, and not one eye to ſeesee each othersother's graces; that they ſhouldshould uſeuse ſpectaclesspectacles to behold one anothersanother's weakneſſesweaknesses, rather thenthan looking glaſſesglasses to behold one anothersanother's graces. EraſmusErasmus telstells of one, who collected all the lame and defective Verſesverses in HomersHomer's works, but paſſedpassed over all that were excellent; ah! that this were not the practice of many that ſhallshall at laſtlast meet in Heavenheaven, that they were not carefullcareful and skillfullskillful to collect all the weakneſſesweaknesses of others, and to paſſepass over all thoſethose things that are excellent in them. Tell me Saintssaints, is it not a more ſweetsweet, comfortable, and delightfulldelightful thing, to look more upon one anothersanother's graces, thenthan upon one anothersanother's infirmities? Tell me, what pleaſurepleasure, what delight, what comfort is there in looking upon the enemies, the wounds, the ſoressores, the ſickneſſessicknesses, the diſeaſesdiseases, the nakedneſſenakedness of our friends? Now ſinsin you know, is the ſoulssoul'ssouls enemy, the ſoulssoul'ssouls wound, the ſoulssoul'ssouls ſoressores, the ſoulssoul'ssouls ſickneſſesickness, the ſoulssoul'ssouls Non Gens, ſedsed mensmensmen's, non Genus ſedsed Genius, Not race, or place, but grace, truly ſetssets forth a ma • n. diſeaſedisease, the ſoulssoul'ssouls nakedneſſenakedness; and ah! what a heart hath that man that loves thus to look? Grace is the choiceſtchoicest flower in all a ChriſtiansChristian'sChristians garden, 'tis’tis the richeſtrichest Jewelljeweljewell in all his Crowncrown, 'tis’tis his Princelyprincely Robesrobes, 'tis’tis the top of Royaltyroyalty, and therefore muſtmust needs be the moſtmost pleaſingpleasing, ſweetsweet, and delightfulldelightful object for a gracious eye to be fixtfixed upon. Sin is darkneſſedarkness, grace is light, ſinsin is hell, grace is Heavenheaven; and what madneſſemadness is it, to look more at darkneſſedarkness, thenthan at light; more at hell, thenthan at Heavenheaven? Jam. 5. 11. 2. 25. 1 Pet. 2. 6. vide. Sin is SatansSatan's work, Grace is GodsGod's work; • work;work• & is it not moſtmost me ••• etmeetmeeet that the child ſhouldshould eye moſtmost, and mind moſtmost his FathersFather's work, &etcc.

Te • ll me Saintssaints, doth not God look more upon his peoplepeople's graces, thenthan upon their weakneſſesweaknesses, ſurelysurely he doth; he looks more at DavidsDavid's and Aſa'sAsa's uprightneſſeuprightness, thenthan upon their infirmities, though they were great and many; he
eyes more Job's patience, thenthan his paſſionpassion, Remember the patience of Job, not a word of his impatience, &etcc. He that drew Alexander whileſtwhilstwhilest he had a ſcarscar upon his face, drew him with his finger upon the ſcarscar; God puts his finger upon his peoplespeople's ſcarsscars, that no blemiſhblemish may appear; ah Saintssaints! thatThat you would make it the top of your glory in this, to be like your heavenly Father; by ſoso doing, much ſinsin would be prevented, the deſignesdesigns of wicked men fruſtratedfrustrated, Satan out-witted, many wounds healed, many ſadsad hearts chearedcheered, and God more aboundantlyabundantly honored, &etcc.

The ſecondsecond Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice2 Remedy. of Satan, is • , ſolemnlysolemnly to conſiderconsider, that love and unity makes moſtmost for your own ſafetysafety, and ſecuritysecurity. We ſhallshallThere was a Temple of Concord amongſtamongst the Heathens, and ſhallshall it not be found among ChriſtiansChristians, that are Temples of the holy GhoſtGhost. be inſuperabilesinsuperabiles, if we be inſeperabilesinseparabilesinseperabiles, invincible, if weewe be inſeperableinseparableinseperable. The world may frownefrown upon you, and plot againſtagainst you, but they cannot hurt you; unity is the beſtbest bond of ſafetysafety, in every Churchchurch and Commoncommon-wealth. And this did that Scythian King in PlutarkPlutarch, repreſentrepresent lively to his 80 Sons, when being ready to dyedie, he commanded a bundle of Arrowesarrows faſtfast bound together, to be given to his Sons to break, they all tried to break them, but being bound faſtfast together, they could not, then he
cauſedcaused the band to be cut, & then they Pancirollus ſaithsaith, that the moſtmost precious pearlepearl among the Romans was call'd unio union. broke them with eaſeease: he applyedapplied it thus; My Sons, ſoso long as you keepekeep together, you will be invincible, but if the band of union be broke betwixt you, you will eaſilyeasily be broken in p • ieces. PliniePliny writes of a ſtonestone in the Iſlandisland of Scyrus, that if it be whole, though a large and heavy one, it ſwimsswims above water, but being broken, it ſinkssinks: ſoso long as Saintssaints keep whole, nothing ſhallshall ſinksink them, but if they break, they are in danger of ſinkingsinking and drowning, &etcc.

The third Remedyremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice3 Remedy. of Satan, is to dwell upon thoſethose commands of God that doedo require youTo act, or run croſſecross to GodsGod's expreſſeexpress command, though under pretence of Revelation from God, is as much as a mansman's life is worth, as you may ſeesee in that ſadsad ſtorystory, 1 Kings 13. 24. to love one another; oh! when your hearts begin to riſerise againſtagainst each other, charge the Commandscommands of God upon your hearts, and ſaysay to your ſoulssouls, oh our ſoulssouls! hathHath not the eternalleternal God commanded you to love them that love the Lord? And this is his VerſeVerse 23. CommandementCommandment, that weewe ſhouldshould beleevebelieve on the name of his ſonneson JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist, and love one another as he gave us commandementcommandment. Oh! dwell much upon theſethese precious commands, that your love may beThe Ancients uſeuse to ſaysay commonly that Alexander and EpheſtionEphestion had but one ſoulesoul in two diſtinctdistinct bodies, becauſebecause their joy and ſorrowsorrow, glory, and diſgracedisgrace was mutual to them both. inflamed one to another. The fourth Remedieremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice4 Remedy. of Satan, is, to dwell more upon thoſethose choice and ſweetsweet things, wherein you agree, thenthan upon thoſethose things wherein you differ; ah! did you but thus, how would ſinfullsinful heats be abated, and your love raiſedraised, and your ſpiritsspirits ſweetnedsweetened one to another; you agree in moſtmost, you differ but in a few; you agree in the greateſtgreatest, and weightieſtweightiest; as concerning God, ChriſtChrist, the ſpiritspirit, the Scripture, &etcc. youYou differ only in thoſethose points that have been long diſputabledisputable amongſtamongst men of greateſtgreatest piety, and parts; you agree to own the Scripture, to hold to ChriſtChrist the Headhead, and to walkWhat a ſadsad thing was it that a Heathen ſhouldshould ſaysay, No beaſtsbeasts are ſoso miſchievousmischievous to men, as ChriſtiansChristians are one to another. according to the laweslaws of the new creature. of Satan is this. Above all, labour to be 1 Pet. 5. 5. cloathedclothed with humility. Humility makes a man peaceable among brethren, fruitfullfruitful in well doing, cheerfullcheerful in ſufferingsuffering, and conſtantconstant in holy walking; humility fits for the higheſthighest ſervicesservices weewe owe to ChriſtChrist, and yet will not neglectIohnJohn 13. 5. the loweſtlowest ſerviceservice to the meaneſtmeanest Saintsaint. An humble heart is a habitation for God, a ſcholarscholarHumility is (conſervatrixconservatrix vir virtutum) ſaithsaith Bernard, that which keeps all graces together. for ChriſtChrist, a companion for Angelsangels, a preſerverpreserver of grace, and a fitter for glory. Humility can weep over other mensmen's weakneſſesweaknesses, and joy, and rejoycerejoice over their graces. Humility will make a man1 TheſThes. 1. 2, 3. quiet, and contented in the meaneſtmeanest
condition, and 'twill’twill preſervepreserve a man from envying othersothers' proſperousprosperous condition. Humility makes a man richer thenthan other men, and it makes a man judge himſelfehimself the pooreſtpoorest among men. Humility will ſeesee much good abroad, when it can ſeesee but little at home; Ah ChriſtiansChristians! thoughThough faith be the champion of grace, and love theethe nurſenurse of grace, yet humility is the beautifier of grace; it caſtscasts a generallgeneral glory upon all the graces in the ſoulesoul; ah! did ChriſtiansChristians more abound in humility,The humble ſoulsoul is like the violet, which grows low, hangs the head downwards, and hides it ſelfeself with his own leaves, and were it not that the fragrant ſmelsmellsmel of his many vertuesvirtues diſcoverdiscover him to the world, he would chooſechoose to live and die in his ſelfself contenting ſecreſiesecrecysecresy. they would be leſſeless bitter, froward, and ſowersower; and they would be more gentle, meek, and ſweetsweet in their ſpiritsspirits and practiſespractises. Humility will make a man have high thoughts of others, and low thoughts of a mans ſelfeself; it will make a man ſeesee much glory and excellency in others, and much baſeneſſebaseness and ſinfulneſſesinfulness in a mans ſelfeself; it will make a man ſeesee others rich, and himſelfhimself poor; others ſtrongstrong, and himſelfhimself weak; others wiſewise, and himſelfhimself fooliſhfoolish. Humility will make a man excellent at covering othersothers' infirmities, and at recording their gracious ſervicesservices, and at delighting in their •• graces; it makes a man joy
in every light that out-ſhinesshines his owneown, and in every windewind that blowesblows others good; Humility is better at beleevingbelieving, thenthan 'tis’tis at queſtioningquestioning other mensmen's happineſſehappiness. I judge, ſaithsaith an humble ſoulsoul, 'tis’tis well with theſethese ChriſtiansChristians now, but it will be far better with them hereafter; they are now upon the borders of the new IeruſalemJerusalem, and 'twill’twill be but as a day before they ſlideslide into IeruſalemJerusalem. An humble ſoulesoul is willinger to ſaysay, Heavenheaven is that mansman's, thenthan mine, and ChriſtChrist is that ChriſtiansChristian'sChristians, thenthan mine, and God is their God in Covenantcovenant, thenthan mine; ah! were ChriſtiansChristians more humble, there would be leſſeless fire, and more love among them thenthan now is, &etcc.

div.head: Now I ſhallshall come to the ReaſonsReasons of the Point, and ſoso draw to a cloſeclose, &etcc.
div.p: THeThe firſtfirst ReaſonReason is, that their hearts1 ReaſonReason. may be kept in an humble, praying,The PhiloſopherPhilosopher had a ball of braſſebrass in his hand, which if he chanced to ſleepsleep with, the fall into a baſonbason awaked him to his ſtudiesstudies; You are wiſewise: and know how to apply it. watching frame; oh! hath Satan ſoso many devices to enſnareensnare, and undoeundo the ſoulessouls of men? howHow ſhouldshould this awaken dull, drowſiedrowsy ſoulessouls, and make them ſtandstand upon their watch? A Saintsaint ſhouldshould be like a Seraphim, beſetbeset all over with eyes and lights, that he may avoid SatansSatan's ſnaressnares, and ſtandstand faſtfast in the hour of temptation. The Lord hath in the Scripture diſcovereddiscovered the ſeveralseveral ſnaressnares, plots, and devices that the DelillDevil hath to undo the ſoulessouls of men, that ſoso being forwarn'd, they may be forearm'd, that they may be alwayesalways upon their watch-tower, and hold their weapons in their hands, as the IewesJews did in Ne • hemiah's time, &etcc.

The ſecondsecond ReaſonReason is, from that malice,2 ReaſonReason. envy, and enmity that is in Satan,Malice cares not what it ſaithsaith, or doth, it may kill or gall. againſtagainst the ſoulssouls of men; Satan is full of envy and enmity, & that makes him very ſtudiousstudious, to ſuitsuit his ſnaressnares and plots to the tempers, conſtitutionsconstitutions, fancies,
and callings of men, that ſoso heehe may make them as miſerablemiserable as himſelfhimself. The RuſſiansRussians are ſoso malicious, that you ſhallshall have a man hide ſomesome of his own goods in the houſehouse of him, whom he hateth, and then accuſeaccuse him for the ſtealthstealth of them: ſoso doth Satan out of malice toAn envious heart and a plotting head are inſeparableinseparable companions. the ſoulessouls of men, hide his goods, his wares, as I may ſaysay, in the ſoulessouls of men, and then goego, and accuſeaccuse them before the Lord, and a thouſandthousand, thouſandthousand other wayesways SatansSatan's malice, envy, and enmity puts him upon, eternally to undoeundo the precious ſoulessouls of men, &etcc.

The third ReaſonReason is drawn from that3 ReaſonReason. long experience that Satan hath had, he is a ſpiritspirit of mighty abilities, and his abilities to lay ſnaressnares before us, are mightily increaſedincreased by that long ſtandingstanding of his; heehe is a ſpiritspirit of above five thouſandthousand yearesyears ſtandingstanding; he hath had time enough to ſtudiestudy all thoſethose wayesways, and methods, which tend moſtmost to enſnareensnare, and undo the ſoulssouls of men: And as he hath time enough, ſoso he hath made it his whole ſtudystudy, his only ſtudystudy, his conſtantconstant ſtudystudy to find out ſnaressnares, depths and ſtratagemsstratagems, to entangle, and overthrow the ſoulessouls of men; when he was but a young Serpentserpent, he did eaſilyeasily deceive, and out-wit our firſtfirst Parentsparents, but now he is grown that Old Serpentserpent, asGen. 3.
John ſpeakesspeaks, HeeHe is as oldeold as the world, Revel. 12. 9. and is grown ueryvery cunning by experience.

The fourth ReaſonReason is, in Judgementjudgement4 ReaſonReason. to the men of the world, that they may ſtumblestumble, and fall, and be enſnaredensnared for ever; wicked men that withſtandwithstand the offers of mercy, and deſpiſedespise the ſpiritspirit of grace; that will not open, though God knocks never ſoso hard by his word, and rod; by his Spirit, and conſceienceconscienceconsceience, are given up by a hand of Juſticejustice, to be1 King. 22. 22. hardnedhardened, deceived, and enſnaredensnared by Satan to their everlaſtingeverlasting ruineruin; and what can be more juſtjust, thenthan that they ſhouldshould be taken, and charmed with SatansSatan's wiles, who have frequently refuſedrefused to be charmed by the Spirit of grace, though he hath charmed never ſoso wiſelywisely, and never ſoso ſweetlysweetly, &etcc.

The fifth ReaſonReason is, That the excellency,5 ReaſonReason. and power of GodsGod's grace may be the more illuſtratedillustrated, and manifeſtedmanifested, by making man able to grapple with this mighty Adverſaryadversary, and that notwithſtandingnotwithstanding all the plots, devices, and ſtratagemsstratagems of Satan; yet he will make them victorious here, and crown them with glory hereafter; the greater, and the ſubtilersubtiler the enemies of the children of IſraelIsrael were, the more did divine power, wiſdomewisdom, and goodneſſegoodness ſparklesparkle,
and ſhineshine; that notwithſtandingnotwithstanding, all their power, plots, and ſtratagemsstratagems, &etcc. yetYet to CananCanaan he would bring them at laſtlast. When Paul had well weighed this, he ſitssits downedown, and glories in his infirmities, 2 Cor. 12. 7, 8, 9. and diſtreſſesdistresses, and SatansSatan's buffetings, that the power of ChriſtChrist might reſtrest upon him.

div.head: The uſeuse of the Point.
div.p: IF Satan hath ſuchsuch a world of devices, ƲſeUse. and ſtratagemsstratagems to enſnareensnare, and undo the ſoulessouls of men, then inſteadinstead of wondering that ſoso few are ſavedsaved, ſetset down, and wonder that any are ſavedsaved, that any eſcapeescape the ſnaressnares of this cunning fowler, who ſpreadsspreads his nets, and caſtscasts forth his baits in all places, and in all caſescases and companies, &etcc.

But this is not the main thing that I intend to ſpeakspeak to; my main buſineſsbusiness ſhallshall be, to ſetset before you ſomesome ſpeciallspecial Rules, and helps againſtagainst all his Devicesdevices, and the firſtfirst is this.

If you would not be taken by any of SatansSatan's Devicesdevices, then walk by rule; heehe that walks by rule, walks moſtmost ſafelysafely,Prov. 12. 28. Gal. 6. 16. Prov. 15. 24. he that walks by rule, walks moſtmost honourably; he that walkewalkswalk by rule, walks moſtmost ſweetlysweetly; when men throw off the
word, then God throws off them, and then Satan takes them by the hand, and leads them into ſnaressnares at his pleaſurepleasure; he that thinks himſelfehimself too good to be ruled by the word, will be found too bad to be owned by God; and if God doedo not, nor will not owneown him, Satan will by his ſtratagemsstratagems overthrow him. Them that keep to the rule, they ſhallshall be kept in the hour of temptation. BecauſeBecause RevelRevel. 3. 10. 3. thou haſthast kept the word of my patience, I alſoalso will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which ſhallshall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth.

Thirdly, if you would not be taken with any of SatansSatan's devices, then labour for more heavenly wiſdomewisdom: Ah ſoulssouls!If men could but ſeesee the fairefair face of wiſdomewisdom with mortal • lmortal eyes, they would be in love with her, ſaithsaith Plato •• . youYou are much in the dark, you have but a little to that others have, and to that you might have had, had you not been wanting to your ſelvesselves. Satan hath his ſnaressnares to take you in proſperityprosperity & adverſityadversity, in health & ſickneſssickness, in ſtrengthstrength and weakneſsweakness; when you are alone, and when you are in company; when you come on to ſpirituallspiritual duties, and when you come off from ſpirituallspiritual duties, and if you are not filled with the Spirit, Satan will be too hard, and too crafty for you, and will eaſilyeasily, and frequently take you in his ſnaressnares, and make a prey of you in ſpightspite of your ſoulessouls; therefore labour more to have your hearts filled with the Spirit, thenthan to have your heads filled with notions, your ſhopsshops with wares, your cheſtschests with

into SatansSatan's ſnaressnares, I do not know what will: And therefore as you would be happy in reſiſtingresisting Satan, and bleſſedblessed in triumphing over Satan, and all his ſnaressnares keepekeep humble, I ſaysay again, keep humble, &etcc.

WatchfulneſſeWatchfulness is nothing elſeelse but the ſoulsoul running up and downedown, tooto and fro, buſiebusy every where; it is the heart buſiedbusied, and employed with diligent obſervationobservation of (Quid inde) what comes from within us, and of (Quid unde) what comes from without us, and into us. I ſhallshall conclude this 7th7th head with this advice: Remember the Dragondragon is ſubtlesubtle, and bites the Elephantselephant'selephants ear, and then ſuckssucks his blood, becauſebecause he knows that to be the onelyonly place which the Elephantelephant cannot reach with his truncktrunk to defend; ſoso our enemies are ſoso ſubtillsubtlesubtill, that they will bite us, and ſtrikestrike us, where they may moſtmost miſchiefemischief us, and therefore it doth very much concerneconcern us to ſtandstand alwayesalways upon our guard.

The third Remedieremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice 3 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider, that the Lord does not in all the Scripture require ſuchsuch and ſuchsuch preparations Rom. 4. 5. Believing, believing in ChriſtChrist is the great thing that God preſſespresses upon ſinnerssinners throughout the Scripture,
as all know, that know any thing of Scripture.

ObjObjObi. But does not ChriſtChrist ſaysay, Come Mat. 11. 28. unto me all yeeye that labour, and are heavy laden, and I will give you reſtrest? To this I ſhallshall give theſethese three Anſwersanswers.
1. That though the invitation be to ſuchsuch that labour and are heavy laden, yet the promiſepromise of giving reſtrest, itsit's made over to comingcoming, to believing.

2. I anſweranswer, that all that this Scripture proves and ſhewsshows, is, that ſuchsuch as labour under ſinsin as under a heavy burden, Math. 11. 28. opened and cleared. and that are laden with the guilt of ſinsin, and ſenſesense of GodsGod's diſpleaſuredispleasure, ought to come to ChriſtChrist for reſtrest; but it doth not prove that only ſuchsuch muſtmust come to ChriſtChrist, nor that all men muſtmust be thus burthenedburdened, and laden with the ſenſesense of their ſinnessins, and the wrath of God before they come to ChriſtChrist. Poor ſinnerssinners, when they are under the ſenſesense of ſinnesin, and wrath of God, they are prone to run from creature to creature, and from duty to duty, and from Ordinanceordinance to Ordinanceordinance, to find reſtrest; and if they could findefind it in any thing, or creature, ChriſtChrist ſhouldshould never hearehear of them. But here the Lord ſweetlysweetly invites them, and to encourage them, he engages himſelfhimself to give them reſtrest. Come (ſaithsaith ChriſtChrist) and I will give you reſtrest.
I'leI'll not ſhewshow you reſtrest, nor barely tell you of reſtrest, but I will give you reſtrest. I am faithfulneſſefaithfulness it ſelfeself, and cannot lyelie, I will give you reſtrest. I that have the greateſtgreatest power to give it, the greateſtgreatest will to give it, the greateſtgreatest right to give it, come laden ſinnerssinners, and I will give you reſtrest. ReſtRest is the moſtmost deſireabledesirable good, the moſtmost ſutablesuitable good, & to you the greateſtgreatest good. Come ſaithsaith ChriſtChrist, that is, Believe in me & I wilwill give you reſtrest. I wilwill give you peace with God, and peace with conſcienceconscience, I will turn your ſtormestorm into an everlaſtingeverlasting calmecalm: I will give you ſuchsuch reſtrest, that the world can neither give to you, nor take from you.

3. I anſweranswer, no one Scripture ſpeaksspeaks out the whole mindemind of ChriſtChrist; therefore do but compare this one Scripture with thoſethose ſeverallseveral Scriptures that are laid downedown in the ſecondsecond Remedieremedy laſtlast mentioned, and it will clearly appear, that though men are not thus and thus burdened and laden with their ſinssins, and filled with horror and terrourterror, ifyet they may come to ChriſtChrist, they may receive and embrace the Lord JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist.

The 4. andandAnd laſtlast Remedieremedy againſtagainst this4 RemedieRemedy. Devicedevice of Satan is, to conſiderconsider, that all that trouble for himsin, all that ſorrowsorrow, ſhameshame, and mourning, &etcc. whichwhichWhich is acceptable to God, and delightfulldelightful to
God, & prevalent with God, flows from faith in ChriſtChrist, as the ſtreamstream doth from the fountain, as the branch doth from the root, as the effect doth from the cauſecause. Zech. 12. 10. They ſhallshall lookelook on Zach. 12. 10. him whom they have pierced, and they ſhallshall mourn for him. All Goſpelgospel-mourningRom. 14. 23. flows from believing; they ſhallshall firſtfirst look, and then mourn. All that know any thing, knows this, that what ever is not of faith is ſinnesin. Till men have faith in ChriſtChrist, their beſtbest ſervicesservices are but glorious ſinssins.

div.head: The fourth Device that Satan hath to keep ChriſtChrist & a ſinnersinner aſunderasunder, to keep a poorepoor ſinnersinner from believing in ChriſtChrist, from embracing of Christ, &etcc. is,
div.p: BY ſuggeſtingsuggesting to the ſinnersinner ChriſtsChrist's4 Device. unwillingneſſeunwillingness to ſavesave; 'tis’tis true, ſaithsaith Satan; ChriſtChrist is able to ſavesave thee, but is he willingwilling? ſurelysurely? thoughThough though heehe be able, yet he is not willing to ſavesave ſuchsuch a wretch as thou art, that haſthast trampled his blood under thy feet, and that haſthast been in open rebellion againſtagainst him all thy dayes • days, &etcc.

div.head: The RemedieRemedy againſtagainst this Device of SatansSatan's is briefly to conſiderconsider theſethese few things.
div.p: 1. THeThe great journey that he hath1 RemedieRemedy. taken from heaven to earth, on purpoſepurpose to ſavesave ſinnerssinners, doth ſtronglystrongly demonſtratedemonstrate his willingneſſewillingness to ſavesave them. Math. 9. 13. I came not to call the Mat. 9. 13. righteous, but ſinnerssinners to repentance. 1 Tim. 1. 15. This is a faithfullfaithful ſayingsaying, and worthy 1 Tim. 1. 15. of all acceptation, that JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist came into the world to ſavesave ſinnerssinners, of whom I am chiefechief.

2. His diveſtingdivesting himſelfhimself of his glory in order to ſinnerssinners'sinners ſalvationsalvation, ſpeaksspeaks out his willingneſſewillingness to ſavesave them; he leaves his FathersFather's boſomebosom, he puts off his glorious robes, and layeslays aſideaside his glorious Crowncrown, and bids adieu • to his gliſteringglistering Courtierscourtiers the Angelsangels, and all this he doth, that heehe may accompliſhaccomplish ſinnerssinners'sinners ſalvationsalvation.

3. That ſeasea of ſinsin, that ſeasea of wrath, that ſeasea of trouble, that ſeasea of bloodFrom the Cradle to the CroſſeCross, his whole life was a life of ſufferingssufferings. that JeſusJesus ChriſtChrist waded through, that ſinnerssinners might be pardoned, juſtifiedjustified, reconciled, and ſavedsaved, doth ſtronglystrongly evidence his willingneſſewillingness to ſavesave ſinnerssinners.

4. His ſendingsending his Ambaſſadorsambassadors early
and late to wooewoo and intreatentreat ſinnerssinners2 Cor. 5. 19, 20. to be reconciled to him, doth with open mouth ſhewshow his readineſſereadiness, and willingneſſewillingness to ſavesave ſinnerssinners.

5. His complaints againſtagainst ſuchsuch as refuſerefuse him, and that turn their backs upon him, and that will not be ſavedsaved by him, doth ſtronglystrongly declare his willingneſſewillingness to ſavesave them. He came to his owneown, 1John 1 John. 11. and his owneown received him not. So in that 5. ofofOf John, v. 40. But yeeye will not come IohnJohn 5. 40. to me, that ye may have life.

6. The joy and delight that he takes at the converſionconversion of ſinnerssinners, doth demonſtratedemonstrate his willingneſſewillingness, that they ſhouldshould be ſavedsaved. Luk. 15. 7. I ſaysay unto Luke 15. 7. you, that likewiſelikewise joy ſhallshall be in heaven over one ſinnersinner that repenteth, more thenthan over ninety and nine juſtjust perſonspersons which need no repentance. God the Father rejoycethrejoiceth at the return of his prodigallprodigal SonneSon. ChriſtChrist rejoycesrejoices to ſeesee the travelltravel ofIſaIsa. 53. 11. his ſoulesoul: the Spirit rejoycesrejoices that he hath another Templetemple to dwell in, and the Angelsangels rejoycerejoice that they have another Brotherbrother to delight in, &etcc.

div.head: The fifth Device that Satan hath to keepekeep a ſinnersinner and ChriſtChrist aſunderasunder, is,
div.p: BY working a ſinnersinner to mind more5 Device. the ſecretsecret decreaſedecreesdecrease and counſelscounsels of God, thenthan his own duty. What needeſtneedest thou to buſiebusy thy ſelfeself about receiving, embracing, and entertaining of ChriſtChrist? Saith Satan, if thou art elected, thou ſhaltshalt be ſavedsaved; if not, all that thou canſtcanst doedo will do thee no good. Nay, he will workework the ſoulesoul not onelyonly to doubt of its election, but to conclude that he is not elected, and therefore let him doedo what he can he ſhallshall never be ſavedsaved.

div.head: Now the Remedies againſtagainst this Device of Satan are theſethese.
div.p:
THeThe firſtfirst Remedieremedy is, ſeriouſlyseriously to conſiderconsider,1 Remedy that all the Angelsangels in heaven, nor all the men on earth, nor all the Devillsdevils in hell cannot tell to the contrary, but that thou maiſtmayestmaist be an elect perſonperson, a choſenchosen veſſelvessel. Thou mayeſtmayest
be confident of this, that God never made Satan one of his PriviePrivy CouncelCouncil, God never acquainted him with the names or perſonspersons of ſuchsuch that he hath ſetset his love upon to eternity, &etcc.

The ſecondsecond Remedieremedy againſtagainst this Devicedevice 2 RemedieRemedy. of Satan, is, to meddle with that which thou haſthast to doedo; ſecretsecret things belongs to the Lord, but revealedDeut. 29. 29. things belongs to thee; thy workework ſinnersinner, is to be peremptory in believing, and in returning to the Lord; thy workework is to caſtcast thy ſelfeself upon ChriſtChrist, lyelie at his feetefeet, to waitewait on him in his wayesways, and to give him no reſtrest till he ſhallshall ſaysay, Sinnersinner, I am thy portion, I am thy ſalvationsalvation, and nothing ſhallshall ſeparateseparate between thee and me.
